Requirements: To apply for the Accounting, BS program, applicants must meet Purdue University's freshman admission criteria. This includes the completion of specific high school coursework: 8 semesters of English, 7-8 semesters of Mathematics (including precalculus, trigonometry, or analytical geometry for business majors), 6 semesters of Lab Science, 6 semesters of Social Studies, and 4 semesters of a Foreign Language. Additionally, applicants must submit the Common Application, which includes the Purdue-specific personal essay and questions, along with official high school transcripts and SAT or ACT scores.

Admission to the BFA in Acting requires an audition and interview. These auditions are held on-campus during the spring semester for admission the following autumn. A current headshot and resume are required for the audition. Applicants must also be admitted to Purdue University and meet general university admission requirements, which include high school coursework and standardized test scores.

The Actuarial Science program is a joint program between the Department of Mathematics and the Department of Statistics. To be eligible for the degree of Bachelor of Science in Actuarial Science, the student must complete at least 120 credit hours of which at least 32 must be in courses at or above the 30000 level and satisfy the requirements of the program. Admission to the program is based on Purdue University's general undergraduate admission criteria, which include high school coursework, GPA, and SAT/ACT scores.

The Advanced Global Technology minor is designed to recognize students who have successfully completed the Purdue Polytechnic Institute Global Technology minor and choose to take additional coursework and/or participate in a second study abroad/global professional experience. To be eligible to complete the Advanced Global Technology minor, students must first complete all requirements of the Global Technology minor (GLBT).

The BSAAE degree requires a total of 130 credits. The School of Aeronautics and Astronautics admits students into the professional program after they have completed the requirements of the First-Year Engineering (FYE) program. A student must have a minimum of 30 semester hours of credit before being admitted to the School of Aeronautics and Astronautics. Admission is competitive and based on the student’s academic record. To be eligible for graduation, students must earn a C- or better in all AAE and required MA, PHYS and CHM courses.

To be eligible for admission to Purdue University, first-year applicants must meet minimum high school course requirements: 8 semesters of Mathematics, 6 semesters of English, 6 semesters of Lab Science (for Engineering Technology: Biology, Chemistry, and Physics are recommended), 6 semesters of Social Studies, and 4 semesters of World Language. Evaluation is based on high school coursework, grades, SAT or ACT scores, a personal essay, and Purdue-specific questions.
Students must earn a C- or better in all AT, MGMT, and ECON courses and any course that is a prerequisite to an AT, MGMT, or ECON course. A minimum of 120 credit hours are required for graduation.
The Aerospace Studies minor is available to all undergraduate students at Purdue University. It consists of the courses listed below.

15 credits. Required Courses: AAS 27100 - Introduction To African American Studies (3.00 credits). African American Studies Electives: Select 12 additional credits of African American Studies courses. At least 3 credits must be at the 30000-level or above (3.00 credits). 9 additional credits (9.00 credits). Note: Students must earn a GPA of 2.0 or higher in the minor courses.

To earn a degree in the College of Liberal Arts, students must complete at least 120 credits, complete the College of Liberal Arts core requirements, and complete the requirements for a major. The Liberal Arts core involves the following: I. Foundations (Mathematics/Statistics, Science, Foreign Language) and II. Exploration (Aesthetics and Culture, Social Science, Individual and Society, Individual and Global Perspective, Global Perspective).

For admission to the Agribusiness, BS program, applicants must complete the Common Application, which includes a personal essay and Purdue-specific questions. Purdue is a test-required institution; therefore, SAT or ACT scores are mandatory for application. High school preparation should include 8 semesters of English, 8 semesters of Mathematics (including pre-calculus or equivalent), 6 semesters of Lab Science, 6 semesters of Social Studies, and 4 semesters of a World Language. To graduate with a BS in Agribusiness, students must complete a minimum of 120 credit hours, including specific major requirements in agricultural economics, business, and quantitative methods.

Admission to the Agricultural Communication major is competitive. Applicants must meet Purdue University's general freshman admission criteria, which includes the completion of at least 15 academic units: 8 semesters of English, 8 semesters of Mathematics (including Algebra I, II, and Geometry), 6 semesters of Laboratory Science, 6 semesters of Social Studies, and 4 semesters of a Foreign Language. Applicants are evaluated based on their high school curriculum, grades, standardized test scores (SAT or ACT), and a personal essay including Purdue-specific responses.

Admission to the Agricultural Economics, BS program follows Purdue University's undergraduate admission criteria. Applicants must submit a completed Common Application, which includes a personal essay and Purdue-specific questions. Required high school coursework includes 8 semesters of English, 8 semesters of Mathematics, 6 semesters of Laboratory Science, and 6 semesters of Social Studies. Purdue University requires SAT or ACT scores for admission. The selection process is holistic, evaluating academic performance, strength of curriculum, test scores, and personal background.

To earn the Bachelor of Science in Agricultural Education (BSAE), students must satisfy University requirements for a bachelor's degree; fulfill Program Major Requirements; General Education Requirements; College of Agriculture Core Requirements; and Concentration Requirements (Agricultural Science and Business or Communication and Leadership). Students must also fulfill a teacher certification requirement. In addition to the GPA required for a BSAE, students must also have a 2.5 average in Agricultural Education (ASEE and ASEC) and content courses. No grade lower than a C- will be accepted for these courses. Students must also pass the CORE Content Area assessments. To be eligible for student teaching, students must have a 2.8 cumulative GPA. Total credits required: 120.

The programs are joint between the College of Agriculture and the College of Engineering and are administered by the Department of Agricultural and Biological Engineering. The faculty are members of both colleges. The Agricultural Engineering and Biological Engineering programs are accredited by the Engineering Accreditation Commission of ABET, http://www.abet.org. Students are admitted to Agricultural Engineering or Biological Engineering after completing the First-Year Engineering requirements.

The minor in Agricultural Systems Management requires the completion of 15 credits of ASM coursework. Of those 15 credits, 9 must be 30000 level or higher. ASM 10500 is not applicable to the minor. At least 50% of the credits used to satisfy the minor must be earned at Purdue University. All courses must be taken for a letter grade and a C- or better is required. A minimum GPA of 2.0 is required for those courses used to satisfy the minor.

Admission to the Agricultural Systems Management (BS) program is based on Purdue University's freshman admission criteria. Required components include a completed application via the Common App, a personal essay, and high school transcripts showing completion of core requirements: 8 semesters of English, 8 semesters of Mathematics (including Algebra I, II, and Geometry), 6 semesters of Laboratory Science, 6 semesters of Social Studies, and 4 semesters of a Foreign Language. Standardized test scores (SAT or ACT) are required for all freshman applicants.

To earn a Bachelor of Science degree in Agronomy, a student must complete a minimum of 120 credit hours. The program offers four options: Agronomic Business and Marketing, Crop Science, International Agronomy, and Soil and Water Sciences. General Purdue undergraduate admission requirements include the completion of a high school curriculum (including English, Math, Laboratory Science, Social Studies, and Foreign Language), the Common App essay, and the submission of SAT or ACT scores.

Admission to the Air Traffic Control, BS program requires high school course completion (English, Math, Lab Science, Social Studies, and Foreign Language), SAT or ACT scores, and a personal essay. A program-specific requirement is that students must be able to obtain a second-class FAA medical certificate. For graduation, students must complete 120 credit hours with a minimum cumulative GPA of 2.0.

The Airframe and Powerplant Maintenance Minor is available to students who have been admitted to the Professional Flight Technology major or the Aviation Management major. Enrollment in this minor is limited. Applications are due the semester prior to the student starting the minor.

Admission to the Airline Management and Operations program is based on a holistic review of academic factors including high school coursework (8 semesters of English, 8 semesters of math, 6 semesters of lab science, 6 semesters of social studies, and 4 semesters of world language), grades in core academic courses, strength of curriculum, and SAT or ACT scores. Personal background and experiences are also considered through the personal essay and Purdue-specific questions.

The American Studies minor requires 15 credit hours of AMST coursework. Required Course: AMST 20100 - Interpreting America (3 credits). Elective Courses: 12 additional credits of AMST courses, 6 of which must be at the 30000 level or above.

To apply for the American Studies, BA program at Purdue University, freshman applicants must meet high school course requirements, including 8 semesters of English, 6 semesters of Mathematics (Algebra I, II, and Geometry), 6 semesters of Laboratory Science (Biology, Chemistry, or Physics), 6 semesters of Social Studies, and 4 semesters of Foreign Language. Purdue is a test-required institution for students applying for the Fall 2024 term and beyond, meaning a score from the SAT or ACT is required. Applicants must also submit a personal essay and answer Purdue-specific questions as part of their application.

Minimum of 18 credits must be earned. Required courses may have prerequisites. ANSC 49100, ANSC 49300 and ANSC 49400 can only be used as 'Other Animal Science courses' and cannot exceed 3 credits towards the minor.

The Animal Sciences program provides students with a strong foundation in the basic sciences (genetics, physiology, nutrition, and products) and the opportunity to apply those sciences to the production and management of animals (including food animals, horses, and companion animals) or the processing of meat, milk, and eggs. The program requires 120.0 credits for graduation and offers five concentrations: Animal Agribusiness, Behavioral Well-being, Biosciences, Pre-Veterinary Medicine, and Production and Management. Applicants must complete the Common App, which includes a personal essay and Purdue-specific questions, and provide high school transcripts and SAT or ACT scores.

The Animation and Visual Effects major focuses on the 3D computer graphics (CG) that are used in the creation of digital animation for the entertainment industry (film, TV, video games), and as a tool for communication and visualization in many other industries. Skills such as 3D modeling, lighting, rendering, and technical direction are emphasized. Freshman applicants must meet general Purdue high school course expectations, which include 8 semesters of English, 8 semesters of Mathematics, 6 semesters of Laboratory Science, 6 semesters of Social Studies, and 4 semesters of Foreign Language.

The minor in Anthropology requires 15 total credits. Required Course (3 credits): ANTH 10000 - Being Human: Introduction To Anthropology. Selective Course (3 credits): Select one of ANTH 20400 - Introduction To Biological Anthropology and Archaeology, ANTH 20500 - Human Cultural Diversity, ANTH 21000 - Technology And Culture, or ANTH 23000 - Gender Across Cultures. Anthropology Electives (9 credits): Select 9 credits of Anthropology courses, 6 credits of which must be at the 30000 level or higher.

The Bachelor of Arts in Anthropology requires a total of 120 credit hours for graduation. Of these, 33 credit hours must be in anthropology, 15 credits of which must be in upper-division (30000-level or above) courses. A 2.0 GPA in the major is required for graduation. All major courses must be taken for a letter grade. Anthropology courses with a grade of C- or lower cannot be used to satisfy major requirements.

To apply for the Applied Agricultural Economics, BS program, students must meet high school course expectations, which include 8 semesters of English, 8 semesters of Mathematics (including Precalculus, Trigonometry, or Calculus), 6 semesters of Laboratory Science, 6 semesters of Social Studies, and 4 semesters of Foreign Language. Applicants must submit an application through the Common Application, which includes a personal statement (essay). Official high school transcripts and SAT or ACT scores are required for admission.

The Applied Leadership degree program is intended for students who have earned an Associate of Science (AS) or Associate of Applied Science (AAS) from a regionally accredited institution. Admission is based on a student’s previous academic record. Students must have at least a 2.0 cumulative GPA for admission into the program.

Applicants must complete the Common Application, which includes a personal essay and Purdue-specific questions. Official high school transcripts or self-reported coursework must be submitted. Admission to the College of Science requires the following high school coursework: 8 semesters of English, 8 semesters of Mathematics (including pre-calculus or trigonometry), 6 semesters of Lab Science (including biology, chemistry, or physics), 6 semesters of Social Studies, and 4 semesters of a World Language. Admission is competitive and based on a holistic review of academic performance and standardized test scores.

To earn the Bachelor of Science Degree in Applied Physics, students must complete a minimum of 120 credit hours, including the Physics, Mathematics, and Science/Engineering courses specified, and satisfy the College of Science Core requirements. Admission to the program requires meeting Purdue University's freshman admission criteria, which includes high school coursework (8 semesters of English, 8 semesters of Mathematics, 6 semesters of Laboratory Science, 6 semesters of Social Studies, and 4 semesters of Foreign Language), the Common App personal essay, and official SAT or ACT scores.

To be competitive for admission to the College of Science, you should have taken at least four years of mathematics (including precalculus or calculus). Purdue University is test-required for students applying for Fall 2024 and beyond. We evaluate you based on: High School Course Expectations, Grades and Test Scores, Personal Achievement, and the Purdue Admission Essay. High school course expectations include 8 semesters of English, 8 semesters of Mathematics, 6 semesters of Laboratory Science, 6 semesters of Social Studies, and 4 semesters of Foreign Language.

The Bachelor of Science (BS) in Aquatic Sciences program is designed to provide students with a strong foundation in the biological and physical sciences, with an emphasis on the ecology and management of aquatic ecosystems. Students must complete a minimum of 120 credit hours. A minimum grade of C- is required for all courses in the Forestry and Natural Resources (FNR) core. Students must also complete the University Core Curriculum and the College of Agriculture core requirements. All students in the Forestry and Natural Resources department are required to complete a 5-week summer practicum.

Total 15 credits. A minimum grade of C- is required in all courses used to satisfy the minor requirements. All ARAB courses must be taken for a letter grade. No more than one course (3 credits) used to satisfy the minor requirements may be taken from a source other than Purdue University. A maximum of one course (3 credits) from a pre-approved list of English-taught courses related to the Middle East may be used to satisfy the minor.

The Architectural Engineering Minor requires a total of 18 credit hours. Completion of the minor requires a minimum GPA of 2.0 in the courses used to satisfy the minor. At least 50% of the credits used to satisfy the minor must be earned at Purdue University. The minor is available to students in the Lyles School of Civil Engineering and the School of Mechanical Engineering.

18 credits required. Required Courses (9 credits): AD 10500 - Design I, AD 11300 - Drawing I, AD 11400 - Drawing II. Elective Courses (9 credits): Select 9 additional credits from Art and Design Studio courses at the 20000 level or above (excluding AD 10500, 11300, and 11400). A minimum of 6 credits must be taken at Purdue University. All courses must be completed with a C- or better.

15 credit hours. Required Courses (6 credits): AD 22600 - History Of Art To 1400 and AD 22700 - History Of Art Since 1400. Art History Electives (9 credits): Nine additional credits of upper-division (30000-level or higher) Art History courses. Note: At least 9 credit hours must be taken at Purdue.

To be eligible for admission to Purdue University, applicants must meet minimum high school coursework requirements, which include 8 semesters of English, 8 semesters of Mathematics (including Algebra I, II, and Geometry), 6 semesters of Lab Science, 6 semesters of Social Studies, and 8 semesters of World Language. Purdue utilizes a holistic review process that considers high school grades, academic strength, SAT or ACT test scores, and a personal essay.

Purdue University uses a holistic review process for undergraduate admissions. Requirements include completion of high school coursework (8 semesters of English, 8 semesters of Math, 6 semesters of Laboratory Science, 6 semesters of Social Studies, and 4 semesters of Foreign Language), SAT or ACT scores, a personal essay, and answers to Purdue-specific questions.
To complete the minor, students should consult with their academic advisor and submit the Asian American Studies Minor Declaration Form.

The interdisciplinary Asian Studies major offers students the opportunity to study the many different aspects of Asia: its history, culture, language, politics, and society. The Asian Studies major consists of 30 credits of coursework, including 15-18 credits in their chosen area of concentration (China, Japan, or General Asia). Students are also required to complete two years of an Asian language (Chinese or Japanese) or the equivalent and at least 15 credits must be at the 30000-level or higher. A total of 120 credits is required for the degree.

The Astronomy minor is intended for students with a strong background in physics. A minimum of 6 credit hours must be taken at Purdue. All courses must be taken for a grade of A, B, C, or D. Courses may not be taken Pass/Not-Pass. Minimum GPA in minor courses: 2.00.

Purdue University requires SAT or ACT scores for individuals applying for undergraduate admission. Freshman admission is based on a holistic review of criteria including high school coursework (Core 40 or equivalent), overall grades, SAT or ACT scores, a personal essay, and answers to Purdue-specific questions. For the Astronomy, BS program, students must complete a minimum of 120 credit hours for the degree and maintain a minimum 2.0 GPA in all Physics (PHYS) courses.

To earn a Bachelor of Science degree, students must complete a minimum of 120 credit hours, which include at least 32 credit hours of 30000-level or higher courses in residence at Purdue University, and have a minimum cumulative GPA of 2.00. All courses used to meet major requirements must be taken for a grade. Courses may not be taken Pass/No Pass. Applicants must submit the Common Application, official high school transcripts, and SAT or ACT scores.

To be considered for admission to the Audio Engineering Technology, BS program, applicants must submit the Common Application, which includes a personal essay and Purdue-specific supplemental questions. Official high school transcripts and standardized test scores (SAT or ACT) are required as part of Purdue University's admission process. The program curriculum consists of 120 credit hours, focusing on the science and technology of sound, including areas such as electronics, digital signal processing, and audio production.

Admission to the Automation and Systems Integration Engineering Technology, BS program is based on Purdue University's general undergraduate admission criteria. This includes a review of high school coursework (meeting minimum subject requirements), academic grades, SAT or ACT scores, and the personal essay provided in the application. The degree requires a total of 120 credit hours for graduation, including core engineering technology courses, math, science, and technical electives.
Program name: Automation and Systems Integration Engineering Technology, BS

Requirements: Admission to the Aviation Management program is based on high school coursework, including 8 semesters of English, 8 semesters of Mathematics, 6 semesters of Laboratory Science, 6 semesters of Social Studies, and 4 semesters of World Language. Purdue University is a test-required institution, requiring either SAT or ACT scores. Evaluation also considers grades, grade trends, strength of curriculum, and a personal essay.

The Biochemistry (AG) program is a program of the Department of Biochemistry within the College of Agriculture. The program requires 120.00 total credits for graduation and is designed to provide students with a strong background in chemistry and the biological sciences. Admission requirements include the completion of high school coursework (8 semesters of English, 8 semesters of Mathematics, 6 semesters of Science, 6 semesters of Social Studies, and 4 semesters of World Language), a personal essay, and the submission of SAT or ACT scores.

To be eligible for admission to Purdue University, applicants must meet the following minimum high school course requirements: 8 semesters of English, 8 semesters of Mathematics (including algebra, geometry, and advanced math), 6 semesters of Laboratory Science (for Science majors, this must include chemistry), 6 semesters of Social Studies, and 4 semesters of a single World Language. Purdue is a test-required institution; applicants must submit SAT or ACT scores. Evaluation is also based on high school grades, the strength of the curriculum, and the personal essay.

Credits must be earned at Purdue University. Credit by examination or transfer credit cannot be used to satisfy the requirements for this minor. Some of the courses listed below may have prerequisites. Please check the course descriptions for more information. Enrollment in some courses may be limited.

To earn the Bioinformatics Minor, students must complete 18-24 credit hours of the following courses: Core Courses (15-20 credits) including Computer Science, Biological Sciences, Mathematics, and Statistics; Elective Courses (3-4 credits). A minimum grade of C- is required for all courses in the minor.

Admission to the Biological Engineering program requires meeting Purdue University's freshman admission criteria. This includes the completion of high school coursework: 8 semesters of English, 8 semesters of Mathematics, 6 semesters of Laboratory Science, 6 semesters of Social Studies, and 4 semesters of a Foreign Language. Additionally, Purdue University requires the submission of official SAT or ACT scores for all undergraduate applicants. Applicants must also complete the Common Application and Purdue-specific essay questions.

Students must complete 16-21 credits. All courses must be taken for a grade (no pass/no-fail). A 2.0 GPA in the minor courses is required. Credit in BIOL 11000 and 11100 or BIOL 12100 and 13100 or equivalent credit is required. Any student at Purdue University is eligible to complete a minor in Biological Sciences, with the exception of students majoring in Biological Sciences.

Admission to the Biology Education Program occurs in three phases: Gateway 1, Gateway 2, and Gateway 3. Information about these Gateways can be found at: https://education.purdue.edu/undergraduate-students/current-students/gateways/. Key requirements include a grade point average of 3.0 or higher in professional education and content courses with no grade lower than a C; completion of Professional Education courses and relevant content courses; and passing the Indiana CORE Assessments for Educators (or equivalent) in both Developmental (Pedagogy) and Content Area(s).

All students who wish to pursue a degree from the College of Engineering must first complete the First-Year Engineering program. Upon completion of the First-Year Engineering requirements, students are eligible to apply for professional status in the Weldon School of Biomedical Engineering. Admission to these schools is competitive and is based on a student’s academic performance in the First-Year Engineering program. The BSBME program requires a minimum of 130 credit hours for graduation.

Admission to the Biomedical Health Sciences, BS program is based on several factors including high school coursework, grade point average (GPA), SAT or ACT test scores, and personal essays. High school course expectations include: 8 semesters of English; 8 semesters of Math (Algebra I & II and Geometry/Trigonometry); 6 semesters of Lab Science (Biology and Chemistry recommended); 6 semesters of Social Studies; and 4 semesters of World Language. Evaluation also considers the strength of the high school curriculum and the applicant's personal background and experiences.

15 credit hours are required for the Biometrics minor. A minimum of 6 credit hours must be taken at the 30000-level or higher. All courses must be completed with a C- or better. A cumulative GPA of 2.0 is required in these courses.

19 Credits. Students interested in the Biotechnology minor should contact the Biology department advisor. Some of these courses have prerequisites. Required courses include AGRY 10500, biological sciences foundations (BIOL 11000/11100 or 12100/13100), Genetics/Cell Biology (BIOL 23100/23200 or 27000 and 28100 and 28600), Biochemistry (BCHM 30700 or CHM 33300 or CHM 53300), and a Biotechnology elective.

The Brain and Behavioral Sciences (BBS) major requires 120 credits. The curriculum is designed to provide a strong foundation in the fundamental areas of psychology and specialized knowledge in the brain and behavioral sciences. Students must complete 120 total credits, which include all of the course requirements listed below.

To be eligible for admission to Purdue University, applicants must complete the following high school coursework: 8 semesters of English, 7 semesters of Mathematics (including pre-calculus or trigonometry), 6 semesters of Laboratory Science, and 6 semesters of Social Studies. Additionally, Purdue requires the Common App personal essay and official SAT or ACT scores for undergraduate admission.

15.00 Credit Hours. Required Courses: ECON 25100, ECON 25200, MGMT 20000 (or MGMT 21200 or AGEC 33000). Elective Courses: 6.00 credit hours from ECON 30100, 34000, 35200, 36000, 36100, 36700, 37000, 38000, 38500, 45100, 46100, 46600, or 47100. Available to non-Daniels School of Business students only. Students must meet Daniels School of Business minor residency requirements and have a 2.0 GPA in minor courses.

Students must complete 15 credits of coursework in French at the 30000-level or above. Required courses include FR 30100 (French Level V), FR 30200 (French Level VI), and FR 42400 (Business French), plus 6 additional credits of French electives at the 30000-level or above. No more than 6 credits may be transferred from a non-Purdue program. A minimum grade of C- is required in all courses for the minor.

To be eligible for admission to the Cell, Molecular, and Developmental Biology program at Purdue University, applicants must meet the following high school course requirements: 8 semesters of English, 8 semesters of Mathematics (including academic/college-prep courses), 6 semesters of Laboratory Science (Biology, Chemistry, and Physics recommended), 6 semesters of Social Studies, and 4 semesters of World Language. Purdue University is test-required; either SAT or ACT scores are required for admission. For the completion of the Bachelor of Science degree, a minimum of 120 credits is required with a minimum 2.0 cumulative GPA.
Program name: Cell, Molecular, and Developmental Biology, BS

Requirements: To be admitted to the professional program, students must have completed the First-Year Engineering requirements, as well as CHM 11600 (General Chemistry) or its equivalent. For guaranteed entry into the professional program, students must have a minimum 3.3 GPA. For students with a GPA between 2.0 and 3.29, admission is on a space-available basis.

Credit Hours: 19.00 to 25.00. The minor requires General Chemistry (CHM 11500 and 11600) or (CHM 12500 and 12600) or (CHM 12901 and 13600); Organic Chemistry (CHM 25500, 25501, 25600, 25601) or (CHM 26505, 26300, 26605, 26400); plus 6 credit hours of 30000 level or higher chemistry courses. A minimum of 6 credit hours must be taken at Purdue University.

To be eligible for admission to the Chemistry, BS program, applicants must complete the following high school coursework: 8 semesters of English, 8 semesters of Mathematics (including pre-calculus, trigonometry, or calculus for the College of Science), 6 semesters of Lab Science (including biology, chemistry, or physics), 6 semesters of Social Studies, and 8 semesters of additional academic electives. Applicants must submit the Common Application, official high school transcripts, and SAT or ACT scores.

The Chemistry, BSCHM program requires 120 credit hours for graduation, maintaining a minimum GPA of 2.0. Applicants must meet Purdue University’s freshman admission criteria, which include high school coursework: 8 semesters of English, 8 semesters of Mathematics, 6 semesters of Laboratory Science, 6 semesters of Social Studies, and 4 semesters of Foreign Language. Purdue University is test-required; applicants must submit either SAT or ACT scores. The curriculum includes the Science Core (e.g., Composition, Foreign Language, Statistics) and the Chemistry Core (General, Organic, Analytical, Physical, and Inorganic Chemistry).

The Chinese minor requires a minimum of 18 credit hours. Required courses include CHNS 20100 (Chinese Level III), CHNS 20200 (Chinese Level IV), CHNS 30100 (Chinese Level V), and CHNS 30200 (Chinese Level VI), plus 6 credits of electives. At least 50% of the credits must be earned at Purdue University. A C- or better is required in all courses used to satisfy the minor. Students must meet all of the requirements of their home college/department and the specific requirements of the minor.

Admission to the Chinese Studies, BA program is based on Purdue University's freshman admission criteria, which include high school coursework (4 years of English, 3 years of math, 3 years of laboratory science, 3 years of social studies, and 2 years of foreign language), overall grades, SAT or ACT scores, and a personal essay.

The program requires a total of 128 credits for graduation. Students must complete the First-Year Engineering (FYE) requirement (29-30 credits) before being admitted to the Lyles School of Civil Engineering. The Lyles School of Civil Engineering core requirements consist of 51 credits. The curriculum is designed to provide students with a broad background in civil engineering and includes courses in construction engineering and management, environmental engineering, geomatics engineering, geotechnical engineering, hydraulic and hydrologic engineering, materials engineering, structural engineering, and transportation engineering.

The minor requires a minimum of 15 credits. 6 credits must be at 30000-level or higher. All courses must be taken for a grade. Required Course (3 credits): Select one from CLCS 23010, CLCS 23100, CLCS 23300, CLCS 23500, CLCS 23700, or CLCS 23900. Electives (12 credits): Select 12 additional credits in CLCS, GREK, or LATN.
Required: High school transcript, SAT or ACT scores, Essay and Purdue-specific questions

A minimum of 18 credits are required for the minor. All courses must be completed with a grade of C- or better. At least 6 credits must be taken at the 30000-level or higher. Note: At least 9 credits must be taken at Purdue-West Lafayette.

Purdue University utilizes a holistic admissions process. Applicants to the Communication, BA program are evaluated based on high school coursework (including 8 semesters of English, 8 semesters of Mathematics, 6 semesters of Laboratory Science, 6 semesters of Social Studies, and 4 semesters of Foreign Language), grades, SAT or ACT scores, a personal essay, and extracurricular activities.

To be admitted to the major in Music (any concentration), students must pass an audition. For the concentration in Composition, students must submit a portfolio of original scores. In addition to the audition/portfolio, students must be admitted to Purdue University.
Requires 18 credits for completion. Open to all students. CIT majors are not eligible for this minor. Students must have a minimum GPA of 2.0 to be eligible to apply for the CIT minor.

To earn the Bachelor of Science in Computer and Information Technology, students must complete 120 credit hours of coursework. Admission to the program is based on a holistic review of the applicant's academic record, including high school coursework (4 years of English, 3-4 years of math, 3 years of lab science, 3 years of social studies, and 2 years of foreign language), SAT or ACT scores, a personal essay, and Purdue-specific responses regarding the choice of major and use of Purdue's facilities.

Students may enter the School of Electrical and Computer Engineering after completion of First-Year Engineering (FYE) requirements. For more information, please see ECE’s transition website: https://engineering.purdue.edu/ECE/Academics/Undergraduates/UGO/T2M.

Students must complete 17 to 20 credits from the following courses. A minimum of 6 credit hours must be taken at Purdue University. Computer Science majors are not eligible for the Computer Science minor. All minor courses must be taken for a letter grade. A grade of C or better is required in each course used for the minor.

To be eligible for freshman admission, applicants must complete the following high school coursework: 8 semesters of English, 8 semesters of Mathematics (including pre-calculus or trigonometry), 6 semesters of Lab Science, 6 semesters of Social Studies, and 8 semesters of World Language. Purdue is a test-required institution; applicants must submit SAT or ACT scores. Admission to the Computer Science major is highly competitive, and applicants are evaluated based on their academic strength, SAT/ACT scores, and the personal essay and Purdue-specific questions included in the Common Application.

Students must have completed the First Year Engineering (FYE) program and be enrolled in a degree-granting engineering program. All prerequisite courses must be satisfied. Required Courses (18 credits): CE 22200 - Biomechanics Or CE 27000 - Introductory Structural Mechanics; CE 32201 - Project Control and Life Cycle Analysis; CE 35000 - Environmental Engineering I Or CE 35500 - Engineering Environmental Sustainability; CE 42100 - Construction Project Management; CE 42400 - Human Resource Management in Construction; CEM 20100 - Introduction to Construction Management.

Admission to the Lyles School of Civil Engineering is through the First-Year Engineering Program. Students who are interested in Construction Engineering and Management (CEM) enter the program after completing the First-Year Engineering (FYE) requirements.

Minor Code: CGRA. At least 15 credit hours are required for this minor. All courses must be completed with a grade of C- or better. Any course used to fulfill this minor must be taken on a graded basis. Required Courses: CGT 11000 - Technical Graphics Communication (3.00 credits), CGT 16400 - Graphics For Civil Engineering And Construction (3.00 credits), CGT 26200 - Introduction To Construction Graphics (3.00 credits), CGT 36200 - Applications Of Construction Graphics (3.00 credits), CGT 46200 - Virtual Design And Construction (3.00 credits).

Students must have a 3.0 cumulative GPA to be eligible for the minor. A maximum of 40 students per year will be admitted to the minor. Students must have completed 30 credit hours. Minor applications will be accepted twice a year (August 1st through September 1st and January 1st through February 1st). All Construction Management (CM) courses are restricted to those who are admitted to the minor or a CM major.

Admission to the Construction Management Technology program is based on the general Purdue University requirements for admission as an undergraduate student. These include high school course expectations: 8 semesters of English, 8 semesters of Mathematics (including Algebra I, II, Geometry, and a fourth year of higher math), 6 semesters of Laboratory Science (Biology, Chemistry, or Physics), 6 semesters of Social Studies, and 4 semesters of a single Foreign Language (recommended but not required). Purdue's admission process is holistic and also considers SAT or ACT scores, grades, and a personal essay.

A minor in creative writing is available for all students at Purdue University, with the exception of English majors in the Creative Writing concentration. The minor consists of 15 credits, including an introductory course (ENGL 20500 - Introduction To Creative Writing) and 12 credits of elective courses chosen from a specific list.

Degree: MFA; Area of Study: Creative Writing; Total Credit Hours Required: 42; Minimum GPA: 3.0; TOEFL: 77 (Minimum subscores: Reading 19, Listening 14, Speaking 18, Writing 18); Writing Sample: Required; Resume: Required; Statement of Purpose: Required; Letters of Recommendation: 3; GRE - General Test: Not Required; GRE - Subject Test: Not Required.

Credit Hours: 18-19. Required: AGRY 10500 (3 cr.), AGRY 37500 (3 cr.), AGRY 50500 (3 cr.). Selectives: 9-10 credits from the following: AGRY 25500, AGRY 33500, AGRY 33700, AGRY 45000, AGRY 48000, AGRY 51500, AGRY 52500, AGRY 53500, BTNY 30100, BTNY 30400, or ENTM 30600. At least 9 credits must be 30000 level or higher. A minimum of 6 credits must be taken at the West Lafayette Campus. Credits from 'Pass/No Pass' courses do not count toward this minor.

Crop science is a professional field that includes the study of plant genetics and breeding, plant physiology, crop production and management, and weed science. General admission requirements for freshmen at Purdue include the completion of 8 semesters of English, 8 semesters of Mathematics (including pre-calculus or equivalent), 6 semesters of Lab Science, 6 semesters of Social Studies, and 4 semesters of Foreign Language. A personal essay and official SAT or ACT scores are also required. The Crop Science, BS program requires a minimum of 120 credit hours for graduation.

To be eligible for admission to the Cybersecurity, BS program, freshman applicants are evaluated based on high school coursework (including English, Math, Science, Social Studies, and Foreign Language), overall grades and grade trends, and SAT or ACT test scores. Purdue University requires a complete application through the Common App, which includes a personal essay and Purdue-specific questions. For this specific program, students must complete a total of 120 credits, maintaining a minimum GPA as required by the Polytechnic Institute.

Minors are only available to students already enrolled in a Purdue degree program. Credits Required: 17. Some courses within the minor, such as DANC 25000 and DANC 35000, have enrollment limitations based on previous course completion or by audition.

To be eligible for admission to the Data Analytics, Technology, and Applications (DATA), BS program, applicants must meet Purdue University's freshman admission requirements. This includes the completion of high school coursework: 4 years of English, 4 years of Mathematics (including Pre-Calculus or equivalent), 3 years of Laboratory Science, 3 years of Social Studies, and 2 years of Foreign Language. Purdue University is a test-required university; students must submit SAT or ACT scores. Admission is competitive and based on high school GPA, rigor of curriculum, and standardized test scores.
Program name: Data Analytics, Technology, and Applications, BS

Requirements: The Data Driven Agriculture minor is designed to provide students with a foundational knowledge of how data and data-driven technology are used in the agricultural industry. To earn the minor, students must complete 15 credits from the specified course list. A minimum of 6 credits must be at the 30000 level or higher. The minor is available to any student at Purdue University.

Purdue University's admission process is holistic. For freshman applicants to programs like Data Science, the following are required: a completed Common Application including the personal essay and Purdue-specific questions, official high school transcripts, and official SAT or ACT scores. Admission is competitive and based on high school course expectations, grades in core academic areas, and the strength of the high school curriculum.

Admission to the minor is through the student’s home college. The program requires 15-18 total credits, consisting of a Foundational Course (TECH 12000 or TECH 12000H), a Required Course (ENGR 20100), and 9-12 credits of breadth and depth selectives.

Admission to the Developmental and Family Science major is based on freshman admission criteria including high school course preparation (8 semesters of English, 8 semesters of math, 6 semesters of laboratory science, 6 semesters of social studies, and 4 semesters of a single foreign language), SAT or ACT scores, academic achievement, and an application essay. The degree requires 120 total credits for graduation, including 36 credits of major-specific courses.

Purdue reviews every application holistically, looking for students who will succeed and contribute to the campus community. Factors considered include high school course expectations (8 semesters of English, 8 semesters of Math, 6 semesters of Lab Science, 6 semesters of Social Studies, and 4 semesters of World Language), grades in core academic courses, strength of curriculum, SAT or ACT test scores, personal background and experiences, a personal statement (essay), and Purdue-specific questions.

Only students with a declared major in Forestry (FORS) or Wildlife (WILD) are eligible for this minor. Students must complete a minimum of 18 credits from the lists below. All courses must be completed with a grade of C- or better. All courses must be taken at Purdue University.

The User Experience Design (UX Design) major will provide students with the skills and knowledge to design digital products and services. Students will learn about the design process, including research, ideation, prototyping, and testing. To earn the degree, students must complete 120 total credit hours, which include 45 credits of program major courses. Students must earn a C- or better in all CGT courses that are required for the major. Admission is based on a holistic review of high school coursework, SAT or ACT scores, and a personal statement.

The Early Childhood Education and Exceptional Needs (ECEN) program is a joint program between the Department of Human Development and Family Studies (HDFS) in the College of Health and Human Sciences and the Department of Educational Studies (EDST) in the College of Education. Students are required to complete 120 credit hours.
Program name: Early Childhood Education and Exceptional Needs, BS

Requirements: The Earth, Atmospheric, and Planetary Sciences minor is available to all students except those in the Earth, Atmospheric, and Planetary Sciences major. The minor consists of 15 credits in EAPS courses as follows: 1. One introductory EAPS course selected from: EAPS 10000, 10400, 10500, 10900, 11100, 11200, 11300, 11600, 11700, 12000, 12500, 12900, 13800, 22100, or 22500. 2. At least 12 additional credits in EAPS courses at the 20000 level or higher. 3. At least 6 of the 12 additional credits must be at the 30000 level or higher. 4. No more than 6 credits of EAPS 39100 or 49100 may be used toward the minor.
Program name: Earth, Atmospheric, and Planetary Sciences Minor

Requirements: To apply for the Ecology, Evolution, and Environmental Sciences, BS program, freshman applicants must complete the Common Application, which includes a personal essay and Purdue-specific questions. Required documents include high school transcripts and official SAT or ACT scores. High school coursework requirements for the College of Agriculture include 8 semesters of English, 8 semesters of mathematics (including pre-calculus or equivalent), 6 semesters of laboratory science (biology, chemistry, and physics), 6 semesters of social studies, and 4 semesters of a world language.
Program name: Ecology, Evolution, and Environmental Sciences, BS

Requirements: Economics Honors majors must have a Major GPA of 3.5 or higher and a Cumulative GPA of 3.3 or higher at time of graduation. The program requires the completion of specific quantitative coursework including Calculus I (MA 16100 or MA 16500) and Calculus II (MA 16200 or MA 16600). Additionally, students must complete a 3-credit Senior Honors Thesis (ECON 49900).

Minors are only available to students with a non-Economics major. 1. A minimum grade of C- is required in each course in the minor. 2. A minimum of 6 credit hours must be taken in residence at the West Lafayette campus. 3. Students must have a 2.0 overall GPA to enter the minor. 4. Admission to the minor requires at least a 2.0 GPA in ECON 25100 and ECON 25200 (or equivalent).

Students must complete 120 credits for the degree. A minimum GPA of 2.0 is required for graduation. Students must complete a minimum of 32 credit hours of coursework at the 30000 level or above at the Purdue University West Lafayette campus. Requirements include Economics Major Courses (30 credits), Other Departmental / Program Course Requirements (44-67 credits), Electives (23-46 credits), and University Core Requirements.

The Economics, BS program requires a total of 120 credits for graduation. The curriculum includes Mathematics requirements (MA 16100 or MA 16500), a Business Core, an Economics Core (including ECON 25100, 25200, 34000, 35200, 36000, 45100), and Economics Electives. Students must maintain a minimum 2.0 GPA overall for all courses taken at Purdue and a 2.0 GPA in all ECON courses. Undergraduate admission to Purdue requires the submission of SAT or ACT scores, and students applying to the Daniels School of Business are expected to have a strong mathematical background, typically including at least one semester of calculus.

15.00-18.00 credits required. A minimum grade of C- is required for all courses used in the minor. Required courses include ECE 20001 (Next Generation Computing), ECE 20007 (Next Generation Computing Lab), ECE 20002 (Electrical Engineering Fundamentals II), and ECE 20008 (Electrical Engineering Fundamentals II Lab). Additionally, 6-9 elective credits of ECE courses at the 20000-level or above are required.
A minimum of 15 credits are required for this minor. Students must earn a grade of 'C-' or higher in all minor courses.

Purdue University is test-required, meaning all students applying for freshman admission must submit scores from the SAT or ACT. The admission process evaluates students based on high school coursework, grades, a personal essay, and Purdue-specific questions. Recommended high school preparation includes 8 semesters of English, 8 semesters of Mathematics (including pre-calculus or calculus), 6 semesters of Laboratory Science, 6 semesters of Social Studies, and 4 semesters of Foreign Language.

Admission to the Electrical Engineering BSEE program requires the completion of the Common Application, including the personal essay and Purdue-specific short-answer questions. Applicants must meet high school course expectations, which include 4 years of English, 4 years of Math (including pre-calculus or higher), 3 years of Lab Science, 3 years of Social Studies, and 2 years of Foreign Language. SAT or ACT scores are required for admission. The program also requires the completion of the First-Year Engineering curriculum before transitioning into the Electrical Engineering major.

15 credits required. Students must earn a grade of C- or better in all courses for the minor. The program consists of 6 credits of required courses (AD 23300 - Electronic Media Studio I and AD 30400 - Contemporary Art) and 9 credits of elective courses chosen from a specified list of AD courses.

Applicants must submit the Common Application, which includes a personal essay and Purdue-specific supplemental questions. Official high school transcripts and either SAT or ACT scores are required for admission. For the Elementary Education, BA program specifically, students must maintain a minimum 2.80 cumulative GPA and earn a grade of C- or better in all professional education, content, and core courses to remain in the program and meet graduation and licensure requirements.

The Engineering and Public Policy Minor is available to all students at Purdue University. This minor is available to any student who has a cumulative GPA of 3.0 or higher. The minor requires a minimum of 15 credits. Only courses with a grade of C or better will be counted toward the minor.

Applicants must submit the Common Application including a personal essay. Official high school transcripts and SAT or ACT scores are required for freshman admission. For the Engineering Technology Teacher Education, BS program, students must complete 120 credits for the degree, with at least 32 credits of 30000-level or higher courses taken at Purdue University. To be eligible for teacher licensure, students must maintain a 2.8 GPA and complete all GATE and EDPS courses with a C- or better.

The Department of English offers a 15-hour minor for students in other departments and schools. To declare the English minor, students must go to their own academic advisor. Requirements include: One course in British literature (3 cr.); One course in American literature (3 cr.); One course in Shakespeare or early modern literature (3 cr.); Two ENGL electives at the 30000-level or higher (6 cr.). Total Credits: 15.

Purdue University expects applicants to have completed the following high school coursework: 4 years of English, 3 years of Mathematics (including Algebra I, II, and Geometry), 3 years of Laboratory Science, 3 years of Social Studies, and 2 years of Foreign Language. Purdue University is test-required, meaning SAT or ACT scores are required for undergraduate admission.

Applicants must submit the Common Application, which includes a personal essay and Purdue-specific questions. Official high school transcripts are required, and Purdue University requires SAT or ACT scores for students applying for Fall 2025 and beyond. High school students interested in Entomology should have a strong background in science (especially biology and chemistry) and math.

The Environmental and Ecological Engineering minor provides a path for students in most other engineering majors to explore EEE. Any student in the College of Engineering who is in good standing is eligible to enroll in the EEE minor. Credit Hours: 18.00.

The BSEEE degree requires 128 credit hours. In addition to the University Core Requirements, the EEE program requires the following: General Education Requirements (24 credits), Mathematics Requirements (18 credits), Science Requirements (15 credits), EEE Core (34 credits), EEE Selectives (21 credits), and Technical Electives (6-10 credits). Admission for freshman applicants also requires completion of a college-preparatory high school curriculum including 8 semesters of English, 8 semesters of Mathematics, 6 semesters of Science, 6 semesters of Social Studies, and 4 semesters of Foreign Language.

To enter the Environmental and Natural Resources Engineering (BSENRE) program, students must first complete the First-Year Engineering Program (30-32 credits). For undergraduate admission to Purdue University, applicants must submit the Common Application, which includes a personal essay and Purdue-specific questions. Required high school coursework includes 8 semesters of Mathematics, 8 semesters of English, 6 semesters of Laboratory Science, and 6 semesters of Social Studies. Purdue University requires SAT or ACT scores for undergraduate admission.
Program name: Environmental and Natural Resources Engineering, BSENRE

Requirements: Admission to the Environmental and Natural Resources, BS program is based on a holistic review of each applicant. Freshman requirements include the completion of specific high school coursework: 8 semesters of English, 8 semesters of math (including algebra, geometry, and advanced math), 6 semesters of lab science (including biology, chemistry, or physics), 6 semesters of social studies, and 4 semesters of a foreign language. Additionally, applicants must submit SAT or ACT scores and a personal essay.

To be eligible for admission, freshman applicants must meet high school course requirements including 8 semesters of English, 8 semesters of Mathematics (including Algebra I, II, and Geometry), 6 semesters of Laboratory Science (Biology, Chemistry, or Physics), 6 semesters of Social Studies, and 4 semesters of World Language. Evaluation is based on academic achievement, SAT or ACT scores, and a personal essay.

The Bachelor of Science (BS) in Environmental Health Sciences (EHS) provides students with the academic and professional skills needed to protect human health by identifying, evaluating, and controlling environmental and occupational hazards. Students in this major take a variety of science courses (e.g., biology, chemistry, physics) and learn how these sciences apply to public and occupational health. Our graduates find employment as environmental health and safety (EHS) professionals in industry (e.g., pharmaceuticals, chemical, automotive, energy, electronics, consulting) and as public health professionals in the government (e.g., EPA, CDC, OSHA, state and local health departments).

The event and meeting management minor is designed to provide students with a comprehensive understanding of the event and meeting management industry. The minor is available to any Purdue student. A minimum grade of C- is required in each course. Total credits: 15. Required courses include HTM 17300, HTM 20200, and HTM 37300, plus 6 credits of selective courses.

Exploratory Studies is a one- or two-semester program (up to four semesters maximum) for students who have not yet decided on a major. During their time in the program, students meet with an academic advisor and take a three-credit career planning course (EDPS 10500) designed to help them make informed choices about majors and careers. Students work with their advisors to select a degree-granting major by the end of their fourth semester.

18.00 Credits Required. Required Courses (9 credits): AGEC 21700 - Fundamentals Of Agricultural Business Management, AGEC 31100 - Farm Management, AGEC 41100 - Farm Business Management. Elective Courses (9 credits): Select three courses from the following list: AGEC 33000 - Management Of Resident Instruction Farms, AGEC 42100 - Consolidating Tax and Accounting for Agricultural Businesses, AGEC 45100 - Applied Policy Analysis, AGEC 31000 - Farm Organization, AGEC 33100 - Principles Of Selling In Agricultural Business, AGEC 41200 - Farm Business Management Workshop, AGEC 42400 - Financial Management Of Agricultural Business, AGEC 42500 - Estate Planning And Property Transfer, AGEC 45600 - Federal Income Tax Law.

The Farm Management major provides students with a strong foundation in business and economics, along with a broad understanding of the technical aspects of agriculture. Students learn to apply economic and management principles to the problems of firms in the food and fiber industry. To earn a Bachelor of Science degree in the College of Agriculture, a minimum of 120 credits is required. Students must complete specific requirements in International Understanding, Communication, Humanities and Social Sciences, Mathematics and Physical Sciences, Biological Sciences, and Agricultural Economics. A minimum cumulative GPA of 2.0 is required for graduation.
A minimum of 15-16 credits is required to complete the minor. Minimum GPA 2.0 (C or better) required in all minor courses. A minimum of 6 credit hours must be taken at Purdue.

A minimum of 15 credits is required for the Film and Video Studies minor. At least 6 credits must be taken at Purdue-West Lafayette. Minor is available to undergraduate students. Minimum GPA required: 2.000. Students must apply for the minor through their primary academic advisor.

Application to the Film and Video Studies, BA program requires the submission of the Common Application, which includes a personal essay and Purdue-specific questions. Applicants must also provide official high school transcripts and SAT or ACT scores. The program requires 120 total credits for graduation, including 33 credits in the major (covering Technical/Production and History/Theory), 33-51 credits in the Liberal Arts Core, and 36-54 elective credits. Students must earn a C- or better in all courses used to satisfy the major.

Admission to the Finance, BS program at Purdue University requires the submission of the Common Application along with a required personal essay and Purdue-specific questions. Applicants must provide high school transcripts and are required to submit official SAT or ACT scores. Recommended high school coursework includes 8 semesters of English, 8 semesters of Mathematics (including coursework through pre-calculus or calculus), 6 semesters of Lab Science, 6 semesters of Social Studies, and 4 semesters of a Foreign Language. For graduation, the program requires the completion of 120 credit hours, a minimum 2.0 graduation GPA, and completion of the Management core and Finance concentration courses.

Purdue University is test-required. Application criteria for freshman admission includes: High school coursework, grades in core academic subjects, strength of your high school curriculum, SAT or ACT scores, and a personal essay. For the Financial Counseling and Planning, BS program specifically, all CSR courses must be completed with a C- or better and a 2.0 GPA is required for graduation.

The Fisheries and Aquatic Sciences minor is open to all Purdue students except those in the Aquatic Sciences and Fisheries and Aquatic Sciences majors. Minor is not available to students on probation. Students wishing to enroll in this minor should consult with the FNR Office of Student Services, FORS 103.

Admission to the Professional Flight Technology major is for the fall semester only. Applicants must meet the general admission requirements for Purdue University. A critical requirement specific to this program is that students must obtain a first-class medical certificate from a Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) approved medical examiner before they begin flight training. The program is highly competitive and is part of the Purdue Polytechnic Institute.

The minor consists of 15 credits. Note: Open to all students except Agribusiness majors. Required courses include introductory economics (AGEC 20300, AGEC 21700, ECON 21000, or ECON 25100), macroeconomics (AGEC 20400 or ECON 25200), AGEC 33000 (Management Methods for Agricultural Business), and 6 additional credits from AGEC courses numbered 30000-59900 (excluding 33000, 33100, 49600, and 49800).

A cumulative GPA of 2.0 or higher is required to graduate with a minor. Required Courses (12-13 credits): FS 16100 - Science Of Food, FS 34200 - Food Chemistry, FS 36200 - Food Microbiology, FS 45300 - Food Processing I. Selective Courses (3-5 credits): Select one or two of the following: FS 34100 - Food Analysis, FS 36300 - Food Microbiology Laboratory, FS 44200 - Food Chemistry Laboratory, FS 44400 - Confectionary Science, FS 45400 - Food Processing II, FS 46700 - Food Plant Sanitation, FS 46900 - Food Packaging.

Selection of students for the College of Agriculture is based on several criteria: high school record (including courses taken and grades earned); standardized test scores (SAT or ACT); personal statement/essay; and leadership and/or school and community activities. Minimum course requirements for admission to the College of Agriculture include: 8 semesters of English, 8 semesters of Mathematics, 6 semesters of Laboratory Science, 4 semesters of Social Studies, 8 semesters of College Prep Electives.

Credit Hours: Minimum 15. Required Courses: NUTR 10500, NUTR 10600, NUTR 10700, and either NUTR 20500 or NUTR 30300. Electives: Select from NUTR courses at the 20000-level or higher to total 15 credits for the minor. Additional Requirements: Minimum Grade of C- is required in each course for the minor. Note: Dietetics (DIET-BS) and Nutrition and Dietetics (NUDI-BS) majors are not eligible for this minor.

The minor in forensic sciences is designed to provide students with a basic foundation in the application of scientific principles to the investigation of crime. This minor is open to all students at Purdue University, with the exception of those majoring in forensic science.
The Forest Ecosystems minor is available to all students except those in the Forestry major.

Credits: 15.00. Students must complete 6 credits of the minor in residence at Purdue. No more than two courses may be used for both the minor and a French major. All courses must be completed with a grade of C- or better.

The French minor requires 12 to 15 credits of course work in French at the 30000 level or above. No more than one course taught in English (e.g., FR 33000) can be used to satisfy the requirements for the minor. All courses must be completed with a grade of C- or better. At least 6 credits must be taken in residence at the Purdue West Lafayette campus.

To earn a Bachelor of Arts in French, students must complete a total of 120 credit hours. The program requires 33 credit hours of French courses above the level of FR 20200. Students must also complete the College of Liberal Arts Core Requirements. Undergraduate admission requires high school transcripts and the submission of SAT or ACT scores.

The Furniture Design minor is available to all Purdue students. It requires 15 credit hours of study. Required Courses (15 credits) include: AD 23000 - Design I, AD 24200 - Furniture Design I, AD 33000 - Design II, AD 34200 - Furniture Design II, and AD 44200 - Furniture Design III.

To be eligible for admission to Purdue University, you must meet the following minimum high school course requirements: 8 semesters of English; 8 semesters of Math (including Algebra I, II and Geometry); 6 semesters of Lab Science (including Biology, Chemistry or Physics); 6 semesters of Social Studies; and 4 semesters of Foreign Language (recommended). Additionally, Purdue University is a test-required institution and requires applicants to submit SAT or ACT scores for admission.

To be considered for admission, applicants must meet Purdue University's freshman admission criteria, which include: high school coursework, overall grades in academic coursework, SAT or ACT scores, and a personal essay. For the General Education: Curriculum and Instruction, BA program specifically, students must complete a total of 120 credits, including University Core requirements (30 credits) and Major Requirements (84 credits). This program is a non-licensure track.
Students wishing to major in General Music (BA) must complete an audition for admission into the major.

Admission to Purdue University and the Genetics, BS program is based on a holistic review of several factors. Requirements for freshman applicants include: High School Coursework (completion of minimum high school subject requirements including English, Math, Lab Science, Social Studies, and Foreign Language), Grades in core academic areas, Strength of your high school curriculum, SAT or ACT test scores, Personal essay (Common App personal statement), and Purdue-specific questions (Supplemental essays).

The Geology and Geophysics major is a flexible program that can be tailored to several different career goals in the solid-earth sciences, including such areas as environmental and engineering geology, petroleum and mineral exploration, and geophysics. The major leads to the Bachelor of Science degree. A total of 120 credits is required for graduation.

The German minor requires the completion of 15 credit hours. Required courses include GER 20100 (German Level III) and GER 20200 (German Level IV), plus 9 credits of German courses at the 30000 level or above. Credits used to satisfy the requirements of a minor may also be used to satisfy other degree requirements (e.g., majors, core, or electives). At least 6 credit hours must be taken at Purdue. Grade of C- or better required for all courses.

Students must meet the degree requirements of both the University and the College of Liberal Arts. Total Credits: 120.00. Students must complete a minimum of 30 credits of German above the 20200 level. GPA Requirement: 2.0 GPA required in all German courses.

The Global Engineering Studies Minor is designed for students in the College of Engineering who want to formalize their global engineering and professional experiences. The minor requires a minimum of 12 credits total, including ENGR 20200 (Global Engineering Professional Preparation) and ENGR 40200 (Global Engineering Professional Seminar). A minimum of 10 elective credits must be completed from the approved global/cultural courses or foreign language courses. A grade of C or better is required in all courses for the minor. Additionally, students must complete an approved international experience (study abroad, internship, or research) of at least 6 weeks in duration.

The Global Food and Agriculture Systems minor is available to any student at Purdue University. 15 credits total. Students must earn a minimum C- in AGR 20100 and a minimum 2.0 GPA in all courses used to satisfy the minor. At least 50% of the credits must be earned at Purdue University. The minor requires completion of AGR 20100, one Global Food Production course (3 credits), one International Agricultural Issues course (3 credits), one International and Cross-Cultural Perspectives course (3 credits), and an International Study Abroad experience (minimum 3 credits).
Program name: Global Food and Agriculture Systems Minor

Requirements: The Global Liberal Arts Studies minor requires 15.00 total credits. Students must complete 3 credits from an Introductory Liberal Arts course (AGRY 12000, ANTH 10000, HIST 10400, or POL 13000). A mandatory study abroad or international internship of at least 3 credits is required. Distribution requirements include 9 credits total: 3 credits from Global Studies and 6 credits from Global Perspectives. A minimum grade of C- or higher is required in all minor courses, and at least 6 credits must be taken at the Purdue West Lafayette campus.

The Global Studies minor is designed for students across the university who want to develop the analytical and practical tools to understand the major issues and problems that affect our world. In addition to a core course, students choose from a list of context courses and language or intercultural options to complete the 12-15 credit minor. Students in the College of Liberal Arts follow the world language requirements of the Global Studies major to complete the language/culture/intercultural portion of the minor. Students in other colleges use the language/culture/intercultural options listed below.

The Global Studies major is an interdisciplinary program that focuses on the study of global issues, processes, and trends. It is designed to provide students with a broad understanding of the world and the complex challenges facing it in the 21st century. Students analyze global issues through an interdisciplinary lens, specializing in a specific world region and developing proficiency in a second language. Application requirements for Purdue undergraduate programs include high school transcripts, a personal essay, and SAT or ACT scores.

Students must meet the following requirements to be admitted into the Professional Program in Graphic Design: Completion of AD 10500 Design I, AD 11300 Drawing I, AD 10600 Design II, AD 22800 Visual Communication Design I, and AD 22900 Design History with a minimum GPA of 3.0 in those five courses.

Admission to the Health and Disease, BS program follows Purdue University's freshman admission criteria. Required high school coursework includes 4 years of English, 3-4 years of Mathematics (4 years including pre-calculus, trigonometry, or calculus are required for College of Science majors), 3 years of Laboratory Science, 3 years of Social Studies, and 2 years of Foreign Language. Applicants must also provide SAT or ACT scores and a personal essay. The program requires 120 credit hours for completion, including foundational courses in Biology, Chemistry, Physics, and Mathematics.

The Health, BS program requires a total of 120 semester hours for graduation. The curriculum includes requirements for Civics Literacy Proficiency, Mathematics, Science, Information Literacy, Oral Communication, Quantitative Reasoning, and Science, Technology & Society. Students must also complete major-specific requirements and concentration-specific courses as outlined by the School of Health Sciences.

The History Minor provides students with an opportunity to delve into the study of the human past and to gain a deeper understanding of the world today. By examining the diverse experiences of people across time and space, students develop critical thinking, research, and communication skills that are essential for success in any field. 15 credits in History are required for the History Minor. At least 9 credits must be at the 30000-level or above. At least 9 credits must be taken at the West Lafayette campus.

To earn a degree from the College of Liberal Arts, students must complete at least 120 credit hours. They must also complete the College of Liberal Arts Core Curriculum, the requirements for their major, and any other requirements specified by their department or the College.

The Horticulture Minor provides students with an opportunity to gain knowledge in the art and science of growing and handling fruits, vegetables, and ornamental plants. 18 credits are required. Required courses include HORT 10100 - Fundamentals Of Horticulture and HORT 20100 - Plant Propagation. Students must earn a C- or better in all courses for the minor. A minimum of 9 credits must be 30000-level or higher, and a minimum of 9 credits must be taken at West Lafayette.

To earn a Bachelor of Science in Horticulture, students must complete a total of 120 credits. The curriculum includes the College of Agriculture Core Requirements (Mathematics and Statistics, Physical Sciences, Life Sciences, Communications, Humanities, Social Sciences, International Understanding, and Multicultural Awareness) and Horticulture-specific core courses. Students must select one of five concentrations: Horticultural Science, Landscape Design, Public Horticulture, Horticultural Production and Marketing, or Turfgrass Science.

Admission to the Hospitality and Tourism Management, BS program follows Purdue University's freshman admission criteria. This includes a holistic review of high school coursework (specifically 8 semesters of English, 8 semesters of math, 6 semesters of lab science, 6 semesters of social studies, and 4 semesters of a foreign language), grade point average, SAT or ACT scores, and a required personal essay.

A minimum of three weeks of an approved international experience outside the United States is required. The program must be approved by the program director. Documentation of completion of the international experience is required. Students must have been a full-time student for two semesters prior to the international experience and be in good academic standing (GPA 2.0 or higher).

The Human Development and Family Studies (HDFS) minor is designed to provide students with a foundational understanding of how individuals develop and how families function within various contexts. 15 credits are required for the minor. Required courses include HDFS 20100 (Introduction To Family Processes) and HDFS 21000 (Introduction To Human Development). Additionally, 9 credits of electives must be chosen from the following: HDFS 28000, 31100, 31200, 31300, 31800, 33000, 33200, 34100, or 34600. A C- or better is required in each course for the minor. A minimum of 9 credits must be completed at Purdue University and a minimum of 9 credits must be taken at the 30000-level or higher.
Program name: Human Development and Family Studies Minor

Requirements: Students must be admitted to the Krannert School of Management or have completed 45 credit hours to enroll in Krannert (OBHR) courses. A grade of C- or higher is required in all courses for this minor. Minimum GPA of 2.0 is required in minor courses.
The minor in Human Rights Studies requires 15 credit hours. At least 6 credits must be taken at the 30000-level or higher. All courses must be completed with a grade of C- or higher.

Purdue University's admission process is holistic. Requirements for freshman applicants include completion of high school coursework (8 semesters of English, 8 semesters of Mathematics, 6 semesters of Laboratory Science, 6 semesters of Social Studies, and 4 semesters of Foreign Language), SAT or ACT scores, and a personal statement. The university reviews applications based on grades, grade trends, and the strength of the high school curriculum.

Admission to the Industrial Design program is a two-stage process. All students are first admitted to the Pre-Industrial Design program. Admission to the Industrial Design program occurs after the first year of study (during the spring semester) and is based upon a review of the student’s first-year course work, a portfolio of work from first-year art and design courses, and a weighted GPA. In the second stage, a limited number of students are selected for the BFA program.

Students may be admitted to the School of Industrial Engineering after they have completed the First-Year Engineering Program (FYE) requirements. The First-Year Engineering Program is a prerequisite for all engineering majors. To be eligible for admission to the School of Industrial Engineering, a student must have completed all of the courses in the First-Year Engineering Program. Total Credits Required: 126.00.

The Industrial Management major combines a traditional management education with a strong technical component. Students complete a concentration in a technical or quantitative field, such as engineering, science, or technology. This program is unique in its focus on integrating management with technical and analytical fields. Students must complete a minimum of 120 credit hours for the degree.

The Innovation and Transformational Change minor is open to any student regardless of major. A minimum of 12 credit hours must be completed for the minor. A 2.0 GPA or higher is required in all courses used to satisfy minor requirements. All courses must be taken for a grade.

The Insect Biology minor requires 15-18 credits. Core Requirements (4 credits): ENTM 20600 - General Entomology and ENTM 20700 - General Entomology Laboratory. Additional Requirements: 11 to 14 credits from any other ENTM courses (specifically ENTM 21000, 21800, 22810, 22820, 25220, 31100, 31800, 44200, or 50000-59999). A maximum of six (6) credits from this minor can be used to meet the requirements of a student’s major, another minor, or a certificate. Minimum of nine (9) credits must be taken at Purdue University.

The minor consists of five courses that are to be taken in sequence: IE 34300 - Engineering Economics, IE 41000 - Intellectual Property Law For Engineers: Introduction To Patents, IE 42000 - Intellectual Property Law For Engineers: Advanced Patents, IE 43000 - Intellectual Property Law For Engineers: Trademarks, Copyrights And Trade Secrets, IE 44000 - Intellectual Property Law For Engineers: Intellectual Property Transactions. Total Credits: 15.00.
Program name: Intellectual Property Law for Engineers Minor

Requirements: The Integrated Business and Engineering (IBE) degree is a unique interdisciplinary program designed to prepare students for careers at the intersection of business and technology. This degree combines a strong foundation in business principles with a rigorous engineering curriculum, providing students with the analytical and technical skills needed to solve complex problems in today’s global economy. The program is a partnership between the Mitchell E. Daniels, Jr. School of Business and the College of Engineering.

To be eligible for admission, applicants should complete the following high school coursework: 8 semesters of English, 6 semesters of Math (including Algebra I, II and Geometry), 6 semesters of Lab Science, 6 semesters of Social Studies, and 4 semesters of Foreign Language. Purdue University requires SAT or ACT scores for admission. Admission is also based on factors such as high school grades, the personal essay, and overall academic strength.

The Interdisciplinary Engineering Studies program is for students who want a solid engineering foundation but who do not plan to practice engineering. IDES provides a pre-professional or a multi-disciplinary education. IDES students must meet with an IDES advisor to develop an individualized Plan of Study. Students are expected to complete the First-Year Engineering program requirements. Students must have a cumulative GPA of 2.50 or higher to be admitted to IDES.

All Art and Design programs begin with a Foundation program. Students are admitted to the Interior Design program through a selective process that occurs at the end of the freshman year. This selection occurs once a year during the spring semester. The selection process includes a review of the student’s performance in the foundation courses and a portfolio review.

The International Studies in Agriculture minor is for students in the College of Agriculture to gain an international perspective through coursework and international experiences. The minor requires 15-21 credits.
