Credits must include: Required Course (AGR 20100 - Communications Across Cultures, 3 credits), Foreign Language (3-12 credits), International Experience (6-9 credits such as Study abroad, International internship or research), and Electives (3-6 credits). Students should contact the International Programs in Agriculture (IPIA) office to discuss the minor and the international experience requirement.

The Islamic Studies Minor requires a minimum of 15 credit hours. This includes a core requirement of ARAB 10100 (Modern Standard Arabic I) for 3 credits and 12 credits of interdisciplinary electives chosen from a specified list of history, political science, religion, sociology, and Arabic courses. Students can count no more than 6 credit hours of Arabic language (ARAB) toward the minor.

The Italian minor consists of 12 credits of courses in Italian above the 100-level. Only grades of C- or higher can be counted towards the minor. No more than 3 credits of transfer credit can be counted towards the minor.
Admission to the Italian Studies major requires a 2.0 GPA or better and completion of the LC 10100 and 10200 or LC 10300 or LC 10500 sequence.

Total Credits: 15.00. Students may not take JPNS courses for Pass/Not Pass for the minor. Students with prior knowledge of Japanese should contact the SLC advisor for placement. Required Courses: JPNS 20100 - Japanese Level III, JPNS 20200 - Japanese Level IV, JPNS 30100 - Japanese Level V, JPNS 30200 - Japanese Level VI, and JPNS 40100 - Japanese Level VII.

To apply for the Japanese, BA program, applicants must complete the Common Application, which includes a personal essay and Purdue-specific questions. Applicants are required to submit self-reported high school grades and standardized test scores (SAT or ACT). Specific high school coursework requirements include 8 semesters of English, 6 semesters of Math (Algebra VI, Geometry, and Algebra VII), 6 semesters of Laboratory Science, 6 semesters of Social Studies, and 4 semesters of a Foreign Language. The Japanese, BA program requires 120 total credits for graduation, including 33 credits in the Japanese major and completion of the College of Liberal Arts Core.
15 credits required. Minimum grade of C- required for each course. At least 6 credits must be at the 30000 level or above. Only 6 credits of Hebrew language can be used toward the minor.

To earn a degree in Kinesiology, a student must complete the Purdue Core, Health and Kinesiology Degree Core, and the Kinesiology Concentration. A total of 120.00 semester credits is required. Kinesiology majors must earn a C- or better in specific major courses, including BIOL 20300, BIOL 20400, HK 25300, HK 25800, HK 26300, HK 36800, HK 37200, and HK 46500. Application requirements include the submission of high school transcripts, the Common Application personal essay, and SAT or ACT scores.

The professional Bachelor of Science in Landscape Architecture (BSLA) program at Purdue University is a four-year plus one summer co-op program. The program is accredited by the Landscape Architectural Accreditation Board (LAAB). Students are admitted to the professional program through a selective portfolio review process after completing the first year of the Pre-Landscape Architecture curriculum.

The Landscape and Turf Minor is available to all students except those majoring in Landscape Architecture, Sustainable Food and Farming Systems, Horticulture, or Turf Management. To complete the Landscape and Turf minor, 18 credit hours must be earned from the courses listed below. All courses must be taken for a grade. A minimum grade of C- is required in each course for the minor.

Students must have completed 30 credit hours and have a minimum cumulative GPA of 2.0. Courses must be completed with a grade of C or better. Students must complete at least 10 credits towards the minor that are not used to fulfill their major's requirements.

The interdisciplinary minor in Latin American and Latino Studies is designed to provide students with a broad and systematic approach to the history, politics, culture, and society of Latin America and of Latino/a communities in the United States. 12 credits. Select 12 credits from the lists below. At least 6 credit hours must be taken at the 30000 level or above. Course credits used to satisfy the requirements for a minor may not be used to satisfy the requirements for another minor.
Program name: Latin American and Latino Studies Minor

Requirements: 15 credits are required. Required Course (3 credits): SOC 32400 - Introduction To Law And Society. Electives (12 credits): Select 12 credits from the following: ANTH 37900, COM 25000, COM 35300, HIST 33300, HIST 33400, HIST 38200, HIST 38300, PHIL 27000, PHIL 28000, POL 32700, POL 36000, POL 41100, POL 43300, POL 43500, PSY 35000, SOC 32600, SOC 32700, SOC 32800, SOC 40200, SOC 41100, SOC 52500, SOC 52600. Notes: A minimum GPA of 2.0 is required in all courses taken for the minor. At least 6 credits must be taken at the Purdue-West Lafayette campus.

Admission to the Law and Society, BA program is based on a holistic review of several factors, including: High School Coursework (8 semesters of English, 8 semesters of Mathematics, 6 semesters of Laboratory Science, 6 semesters of Social Studies, and 4 semesters of Foreign Language), Grades in Academic Coursework, Strength of High School Curriculum, Trends in Achievement, SAT or ACT scores, and a Personal Essay.

The Learning Sciences in Educational Studies minor is available to any student at Purdue University with an interest in learning and education. A grade of C- or higher is required in all courses used for the minor.
Program name: Learning Sciences in Educational Studies Minor

Requirements: The LGBT Studies Minor is an interdisciplinary minor that requires 15 credit hours. Students must take WGSS 28200: Introduction to LGBT Studies and 12 credits from the following list. No more than two courses (6 credits) may be taken in any one department (e.g. SOC, HIST, ENGL). All courses must be completed with a grade of C- or better.

To apply for the Bachelor of Arts in the College of Liberal Arts at Purdue University, freshman applicants must meet high school course expectations, which include 8 semesters of English, 8 semesters of Mathematics, 6 semesters of Lab Science, 6 semesters of Social Studies, and 4 semesters of a World Language. Additionally, Purdue requires a personal essay submitted via the Common Application and official SAT or ACT scores. Admission is determined through a holistic review process that considers academic performance, test scores, and personal background.

The Linguistics minor provides students with a general introduction to the field of linguistics, plus a solid foundation in the two primary areas of linguistics (phonology and morphology/syntax). Students then have the opportunity to take two additional courses in areas of linguistics that most interest them. Required Courses (9 credits): LING 20100 - Introduction To Linguistics, LING 31100 - Fundamentals Of Phonology, LING 31500 - Fundamentals Of Morphology And Syntax. Elective Courses (6 credits): Select two courses from the following list: LING 31200, LING 31300, LING 31700, LING 32100, LING 36800, LING 39800, LING 49000, LING 49800, LING 50000-level and above, or SLC 30000-level and above. Total Credits: 15.00.

To apply for the Linguistics, BA program, applicants must submit the Common Application or the Purdue application, which includes Purdue-specific essay questions. Applicants must meet high school course expectations, which include 8 semesters of English, 8 semesters of Mathematics, 6 semesters of Lab Science, 6 semesters of Social Studies, and 4 semesters of a Foreign Language. Additionally, Purdue University requires the submission of SAT or ACT scores for freshman admission.

2.0 average GPA for all minor courses. All courses must be taken for a grade (no P/N). A minimum of 9 credits must be completed at Purdue West Lafayette. The Management minor is not available to students in the School of Management. Students should consult with their academic advisor to add the minor.

Admission to the Mitchell E. Daniels, Jr. School of Business is competitive and based on a holistic review of academic achievement (high school coursework and grades), standardized test scores, and personal background. For students applying for the Fall 2024 term and beyond, Purdue University is test-required (SAT or ACT). To earn the Bachelor of Science degree in Management, students must complete a minimum of 120 credit hours, including University Core requirements, the Mitchell E. Daniels, Jr. School of Business Core, and Management Major courses.

The Manufacturing Minor is designed for students in Management, Science, Technology and Engineering to provide them with the opportunity to explore technical, economic, and management issues related to manufacturing. Students must complete 18 credit hours.

To be considered for admission, you must submit: a completed Common Application, the Purdue-specific questions and essay, self-reported or official high school transcripts, and SAT or ACT scores. Purdue is a test-required university. For the 2024-25 application cycle, we require either the SAT or ACT for all freshman applicants.

Minor Code: MTLS. 15-16 Credit Hours. Students must have a cumulative GPA of 2.0 or higher. Students must receive a 'C' or higher in MSE 23000 to move on to selectives. Minor is not available to Materials Science and Engineering majors.

All students must complete the First-Year Engineering program requirements before entering the Materials Science and Engineering program. The program requires a minimum of 126 credits for graduation, which includes core engineering courses, 27 credits of MSE Technical Electives, and 18 credits of General Education Electives. Additionally, students must earn a minimum grade of C- in specific core courses: MSE 23000, 23500, 26000, 27000, 33500, 37000, and 38200.

To be eligible for admission to the Mathematical Economics, BS program, first-year applicants must meet Purdue's high school course expectations, which include 8 semesters of English, 8 semesters of Mathematics (including pre-calculus or higher), 6 semesters of Laboratory Science, 6 semesters of Social Studies, and 4 semesters of a World Language. Additionally, Purdue is a test-required institution, requiring the submission of SAT or ACT scores, and applicants must complete a personal essay as part of the Common Application.

15-18 Credits Required. All courses for the Mathematics minor must be completed with a grade of C- or better. At least 6 credits must be taken at Purdue-West Lafayette. Any course required for the minor may be used as an elective in any other major or minor. No course may be used to satisfy more than one requirement for the minor.

To be eligible for admission to the Mathematics, BS program at Purdue University, applicants must meet general freshman admission criteria. This includes the completion of a high school curriculum with 8 semesters of English, 8 semesters of Mathematics (including pre-calculus or trigonometry), 6 semesters of Laboratory Science, 6 semesters of Social Studies, and 4 semesters of Foreign Language. Additionally, Purdue requires the submission of official SAT or ACT scores and the completion of the personal essay provided in the Common Application.

Admission to the Mechanical Engineering Technology BS program requires completion of high school coursework including 8 semesters of English, 8 semesters of Mathematics (including Pre-calculus or higher), 6 semesters of Lab Science (Chemistry and Physics are recommended), 6 semesters of Social Studies, and 4 semesters of World Language. The program itself requires 120 credit hours for graduation and is accredited by the Engineering Technology Accreditation Commission of ABET.

To earn the degree of Bachelor of Science in Mechanical Engineering (BSME), a student must complete the 128-credit hour program. To be eligible for graduation, a student must earn a minimum cumulative GPA of 2.0 in all courses taken at Purdue University and a minimum cumulative GPA of 2.0 in all ME courses (ME GPA). Most students are admitted to the School of Mechanical Engineering after completing the First-Year Engineering (FYE) program. General freshman application requirements for Purdue include the Common Application, a personal essay, Purdue-specific questions, high school transcripts, and SAT or ACT scores.

The Medical Laboratory Sciences (MLS) program consists of three years of pre-professional study on the Purdue campus followed by one year (usually 12 months) of clinical laboratory curriculum in a program accredited by the National Accrediting Agency for Clinical Laboratory Sciences (NAACLS). Students must apply for the clinical year of study during the fall of their junior year. Admission to the clinical year is competitive and is not guaranteed.

To apply for the Medieval and Renaissance Studies, BA program, applicants must submit the Common Application, official high school transcripts, and SAT or ACT scores. Recommended high school coursework includes 8 semesters of English, 6-8 semesters of Mathematics (including Algebra I, II, and Geometry), 6 semesters of Laboratory Science, 6 semesters of Social Studies, and 4 semesters of a World Language. Students are also required to complete Purdue-specific essay questions as part of the application process.

Admission to the Mechatronics Engineering Technology program is based on Purdue University's freshman admission criteria. Applicants are required to submit high school transcripts and SAT or ACT scores. The high school curriculum should include 8 semesters of English, 8 semesters of Mathematics (including pre-calculus or calculus), 6 semesters of Laboratory Science, 6 semesters of Social Studies, and 4 semesters of Foreign Language. The program itself is a STEM-certified program that requires 120 credit hours for completion.

The Meteorology and Climatology program is designed to provide students with a solid foundation in the study of the atmosphere and its phenomena. To apply as a freshman to Purdue University, applicants must submit the Common Application, which includes a personal essay and Purdue-specific questions. Purdue is a test-required institution for students applying for 2024 and beyond; therefore, SAT or ACT scores are required. For graduation, the program requires 120 semester hours and a minimum 2.0 graduation GPA.

Applicants for the Microbiology, BS program must meet Purdue University's freshman admission criteria, which include the completion of high school coursework (4 years of English, 4 years of math, 3 years of lab science, etc.), submission of SAT or ACT scores, and the Common App personal essay along with Purdue-specific supplemental questions. The degree requires a total of 120 credit hours for graduation, including the Biology Core (21-23 credits), Microbiology Emphasis (16-20 credits), and supporting coursework in Chemistry, Physics, and Mathematics. A minimum cumulative GPA of 2.00 is required.

The Military Science and Leadership Minor requires a total of 18.00 credits. Required courses include MILT 10100, MILT 10200, MILT 20100, MILT 20200, MILT 30100, MILT 30200, MILT 40100, and MILT 40200. Additionally, Army ROTC Cadets must complete a summer internship (MILT 39500) between the junior and senior year.

Students normally apply for admission to the Multidisciplinary Engineering (MDE) or Interdisciplinary Engineering (IDE) programs during their second semester in First-Year Engineering. After being admitted to the School of Engineering Education, the student is assigned a faculty advisor to assist in the development of a plan of study.

The Music History and Theory Minor is available to all undergraduate students at Purdue. A grade of C- or better is required in all courses for the minor. Students may use a maximum of 6 credits from other institutions to satisfy the requirements for this minor. No audition is required for this minor. Course Prerequisites: Enrollment in MUS 16100 (Music Theory I) requires credit for MUS 13200 (Music Theory Fundamentals) or a passing score on the Theory Placement Exam.

To be admitted to the Music Theory, BA program, applicants must meet the general freshman admission requirements for Purdue University. This includes the completion of a high school curriculum with 8 semesters of English, 8 semesters of Mathematics, 6 semesters of Laboratory Science, 6 semesters of Social Studies, and 4 semesters of a Foreign Language. Admission is also based on academic achievement (GPA), SAT or ACT scores, and a personal essay. Specifically for the Music Theory major, an audition is not required.

This minor is available to any student at Purdue University. The Native American and Indigenous Studies minor consists of 15-18 credit hours. Students must complete one required core course (3 credits) and 12-15 credits of electives.
Program name: Native American and Indigenous Studies Minor

Requirements: 18.00 Credit Hours. The Natural Resources and Environmental Science minor is available to students in all colleges. Students must complete a minimum of 18 credit hours of coursework. A maximum of 6 credits from a student’s major or another minor can be used to satisfy the requirements for this minor. Course requirements include NRES 20000 - Introduction To Environmental Science and NRES 29000 - Introduction To Natural Resources And Environmental Science Academic Career.
Program name: Natural Resources and Environmental Science Minor

Requirements: The Naval Science minor is available to students who have been admitted into the Naval Reserve Officers Training Corps (NROTC). The minor requires 18 credits of Naval Science (NS) courses. A minimum of 18 credits must be earned in Naval Science courses with a grade of C- or better. All NS courses are 2-3 credit hours. Required courses include: NS 11000, NS 21300, NS 21400, NS 31000, NS 31100, NS 41000, NS 41100, NS 41200, and NS 41300.

The program in neurobiology and physiology offers students a strong background in the basic disciplines of biology, including cell biology, genetics, and molecular biology. In addition, students take a variety of courses in neurobiology, physiology, and related areas. The program provides an excellent foundation for students planning to attend medical, dental, or veterinary school, as well as those planning to pursue graduate study in a variety of fields. A minimum of 120 credit hours is required for graduation, and the Department of Biological Sciences requires a C- or better in all BIOL courses used to satisfy degree requirements.

The minor in nuclear engineering is open to any student at Purdue University. A student must complete 12 credit hours of nuclear engineering (NUCL) courses at the 20000 level or above. At least 6 of these credit hours must be at the 30000 level or above. All courses must be taken for a grade. A GPA of 2.0 or better must be achieved in the courses used for the minor.

The First-Year Engineering program is the entry point for all beginning engineering students. In this program, students complete a common first-year curriculum which includes chemistry, calculus, physics, and English composition, as well as an introduction to engineering. After completing the First-Year Engineering requirements, students can apply for transition into the School of Nuclear Engineering. The School of Nuclear Engineering requires a total of 126 credit hours for the Bachelor of Science in Nuclear Engineering degree.

Admission is competitive and is based on high school record and SAT or ACT scores. The number of students admitted to the nursing program is limited by the availability of faculty and clinical facilities. Enrollment in the professional nursing program begins in the freshman year. To be considered for admission, students must have a minimum of: 4 years of English, 4 years of math (including pre-calculus or equivalent), 3 years of lab science (including biology and chemistry), 3 years of social studies, and 2 years of foreign language. High school students are encouraged to complete as much biology and chemistry as possible.
Enrollment in the Nutrition Minor is open to any student currently enrolled at Purdue University. A grade of C- or higher is required in all NUTR courses.

Admission to the Nutrition Science, BS program at Purdue University requires a completed Common Application, including a personal essay. Applicants must provide high school transcripts showing completion of 8 semesters of English and Math, 6 semesters of Lab Science and Social Studies, and 4 semesters of Foreign Language. Purdue University is a test-required institution; therefore, all undergraduate applicants must submit official SAT or ACT scores for admission consideration.

Purdue’s admission process is holistic. Requirements for freshman applicants include high school course expectations (8 semesters of English, 8 of Math, 6 of Lab Science, 6 of Social Studies, and 4 of Foreign Language), SAT or ACT scores, and a personal essay. The application is submitted through the Common App, including Purdue-specific questions.

To finish the Occupational Health Sciences major, a student must complete a minimum of 120.00 semester credits. A minimum cumulative GPA of 2.0 is required for graduation. A minimum grade of C- or better is required in all Health Sciences (HSCI) courses. General undergraduate admission to Purdue University requires the completion of high school coursework (8 semesters of English, 8 semesters of Math, 6 semesters of Lab Science, 6 semesters of Social Studies, and 8 semesters of World Language recommended) and the submission of SAT or ACT scores for students applying for Fall 2024 and beyond.

Total Credits: 18.00. Required courses include TLI 11200 - Foundations Of Organizational Leadership, TLI 15200 - Business Principles For Organizational Leadership, TLI 21300 - Project Management, and TLI 25300 - Principles Of Personnel Management. Additionally, 6 credits of selective courses are required. All courses must be completed with a grade of C- or better. Transfer credit for TLI 11200, TLI 15200, TLI 21300, and TLI 25300 is not accepted. These courses must be taken at a Purdue University campus.

To earn a Bachelor of Science degree in the Purdue Polytechnic Institute, students must satisfy the following requirements: a minimum of 120 credit hours, a minimum cumulative GPA of 2.00, and at least 32 credit hours of Purdue coursework at the 30000 level or higher. Applicants must also meet Purdue University undergraduate admission criteria, which include submission of the Common Application, personal essay, and Purdue-specific responses. High school course expectations include 8 semesters of English, 8 semesters of Math, 6 semesters of Lab Science, 6 semesters of Social Studies, and 4 semesters of a Foreign Language.
The Peace Studies Minor requires a total of 15 credit hours. A GPA of 2.0 is required in courses for the minor. At least 6 of these 15 credits must be taken at Purdue.

The Department of Food Science and Department of Animal Sciences offer a Pet Food Processing minor to undergraduate students interested in careers in the pet food industry. This minor is designed to provide a background in pet food processing, nutrition, and safety. Contact the Department of Food Science for more information or to apply for the minor. 15 credits are required.

To be eligible for admission to the BSPS program, students must meet the general admission requirements of Purdue University. Admission is competitive and based on several factors, including: High school grades, Strength of high school curriculum, SAT or ACT scores, and student's essay and Purdue-specific questions. Recommended high school coursework includes 8 semesters of English, 8 semesters of Math, 6 semesters of Lab Science, 6 semesters of Social Studies, and 4 semesters of Foreign Language.

The Bachelor of Arts in Philosophy provides students with a broad and rigorous training in the history of philosophy, its main figures and movements, as well as its core areas (logic, metaphysics, epistemology, and ethics). Philosophy students learn to analyze and evaluate arguments, to read carefully and critically, and to write with clarity and precision. The program requires a minimum of 120 credit hours for graduation.

Minimum Credits: 18-21. Students must complete the following core courses: PHYS 17200 - Modern Mechanics and PHYS 27200 - Electric And Magnetic Interactions (or equivalents). Students who take PHYS 22000, PHYS 22100, PHYS 23300, or PHYS 23400 should contact the physics departmental advisor regarding equivalent courses. Electives: Students must select 6-9 credits from the following courses: PHYS 31000, PHYS 32200, PHYS 33000, PHYS 34000, PHYS 34200, PHYS 34400, PHYS 36000, PHYS 41000, PHYS 41100, PHYS 41600, PHYS 41700, PHYS 42200, PHYS 43000, PHYS 43100, PHYS 45000, PHYS 46000, PHYS 46100, and any PHYS 50000-level course. Other Requirements: PHYS 23500 and PHYS 24100/PHYS 25100/PHYS 26100 are not applicable toward the minor. PHYS 34200L and PHYS 34400L are not applicable toward the minor. No more than 4 credits of lower-level (10000 or 20000) courses taken elsewhere may be used toward the minor. No more than 3 credits of upper-level (30000, 40000, or 50000) courses taken elsewhere may be used toward the minor.

Application requirements for the Physics, BS program include the submission of the Common Application, which requires a personal statement (essay). Purdue University is test-required, meaning official SAT or ACT scores must be submitted for freshman admission. High school course requirements include 8 semesters of English, 8 semesters of Mathematics (including pre-calculus or equivalent), 6 semesters of Laboratory Science, 6 semesters of Social Studies, and 8 semesters of Foreign Language. Once admitted, students must complete a minimum of 120 credits, maintain a minimum cumulative GPA of 2.0, and fulfill the College of Science Core Curriculum requirements to graduate.

To apply for the Bachelor of Science in Planetary Sciences, students must submit the Common Application, which includes a personal essay and response to Purdue-specific questions. Applicants must also provide high school transcripts or use the Self-Reported Academic Record (SRAR). Purdue University is a test-required institution, and all students applying for undergraduate admission are required to submit SAT or ACT scores. The program curriculum includes core requirements in Earth, Atmospheric, and Planetary Sciences, along with significant coursework in Mathematics, Physics, and Chemistry.

15.00 semester credits are required for the Plant Biology Minor. Required Courses: BTNY 12000 - Introduction To Plant Science or BTNY 12100 - Introduction To Plant Science (3 credits) and AGRY 32000 - Genetics or BIOL 44000 - Phylogenetic Biology (3 credits). Additionally, 9 credits must be chosen from a specific list of approved courses including: AGRY 32100, AGRY 43500, BIOL 23100, BIOL 23200, BIOL 24100, BIOL 24200, BIOL 30100, BIOL 43800, BIOL 43900, BIOL 48300, BIOL 53300, BTNY 11000, BTNY 21000, BTNY 21100, BTNY 30100, BTNY 30400, BTNY 55100, BTNY 55300, BTNY 56000, ENTM 31100, FNR 33100, FNR 43411, HORT 20100, HORT 30100.

120.00 Semester Credits required for graduation. The Plant Genetics, Breeding, and Biotechnology curriculum provides a base in the plant sciences, including plant biology, genetics, and molecular biology. The core curriculum focuses on plant breeding, molecular genetics, and biotechnology. Students are also required to take a set of core courses in chemistry and mathematics. Students must have a 2.0 overall GPA to graduate. Application requirements include high school coursework, SAT or ACT scores, and the Common App essay/Purdue-specific questions.
Program name: Plant Genetics, Breeding, and Biotechnology, BS

Requirements: A minimum of 12 credits. Grade of C- or better in each course used for the minor. A minimum of six credit hours must be taken at Purdue.

15 credits required. At least a C- must be earned in all courses used for the minor. At least 9 credit hours must be taken at the West Lafayette campus. Required courses include POL 10100, one of (POL 12000, POL 13000, or POL 14100), POL 15000, and 6 credits of POL courses at the 30000 level or above.

To earn the Bachelor of Arts in Political Science, students must complete 120 total credits, including 33 credits specifically for the major. Admission requires completion of the Common Application, which includes a personal statement and Purdue-specific short-answer questions. Applicants must provide high school transcripts and official SAT or ACT scores. The program requires completion of the University Core Curriculum and the College of Liberal Arts Core Requirements, including proficiency in a foreign language through the level of 202nd-semester equivalent.

15 semester hours required. All PTGS credits must be C- or better. At least 6 credits must be taken in residence (on the West Lafayette campus). Students may also take PTGS 10500 - Accelerated Portuguese for Speakers of Spanish (3 cr.) as a substitute for PTGS 10100 and PTGS 10200.

Students are admitted to Pre-Communication if they do not meet the direct admission requirements for the Lamb School of Communication. CODOing into Pre-Communication requires a 2.0 GPA. To move from Pre-Communication to a major in the Lamb School of Communication, students must complete at least 30 credit hours of college-level coursework, at least 12 of which must be from Purdue West Lafayette, and have a minimum 3.0 cumulative Purdue GPA.

Pre-dentistry, pre-medicine, and pre-veterinary medicine are not majors at Purdue University. Students interested in these areas should choose a major and also complete the specific requirements for the professional school of their choice. Most students in these areas choose a major in the College of Agriculture, the College of Health and Human Sciences, or the College of Science. Pre-professional students are expected to maintain high standards of scholarship and to exhibit the characteristics of integrity and maturity. Students should visit Pre-Professional Advising (PPA) early in their first year at Purdue.

Pre-law is not a major at Purdue University. It is a set of activities and advising services that help students prepare for law school. Students interested in law school are encouraged to choose a major in an area that interests them and to pursue a rigorous course of study that develops their analytical and communication skills.

Pre-medicine is NOT a major. Students should choose a major in which they have an interest and can excel. Any major is acceptable, as long as the student completes the required prerequisite courses for medical school. Admissions committees evaluate a candidate’s application based on several factors: Academic Excellence, Admissions Test (MCAT), and Co-curricular activities including Clinical/Direct Patient Care Experience, Service/Volunteer Experience, Research, and Leadership/Involvement. Although each medical school has its own set of prerequisites, most require two semesters each of: General Biology, General Chemistry, Organic Chemistry, Physics, and English.

Minimum Semester Credits: 12; Minimum Cumulative GPA: 3.0; Minimum Program GPA: 3.0. Other: 3.0 CUM GPA and 3.0 Program GPA. Student must have a 'C' or better in any Nursing program course already completed. A grade of 'C' or better in the following courses (as applicable): BIOL 11000, 20300, 20400, 22100; CHM 11100, 11200, 11500, 11600; PSY 12000; HDFS 21000; SOC 10000; ENGL 10600, 10800; COM 11400; MA 15300 or higher; STAT 30100; NUTR 30300. Space in the Pre-Nursing and Nursing majors is limited. CODO is a competitive process; meeting the minimum requirements does not guarantee CODO into the major.

Students who are interested in the Doctor of Pharmacy (PharmD) program usually choose Pre-Pharmacy as their major for their first two years. This is not a degree-granting program. After completion of these two years of study, students may apply to the Doctor of Pharmacy program. Pre-Pharmacy requires 63-65 credits. All courses must be completed with a grade of C- or better. All required courses must be taken for a grade, not Pass/Not Pass.

Purdue University provides several avenues for students to prepare for graduate study in Physical Therapy. Students are encouraged to pursue a bachelor’s degree in a field that is of interest to them and includes the required prerequisites for graduate school. Pre-physical therapy requirements include: two semesters of general chemistry with labs; two semesters of general biology with labs; two semesters of general physics with labs; two semesters of anatomy and physiology with labs; and one semester of psychology, and one semester of statistics. Other courses may be required depending on the specific graduate program. In addition to a strong academic record, students should seek opportunities to gain clinical experience in a physical therapy setting and participate in extracurricular activities.

Pre-physician assistant students choose a degree-granting major in any of the colleges at Purdue University. While physician assistant programs do not require a specific major, students must complete the required and recommended prerequisite coursework for each physician assistant program to which they plan to apply. Extracurricular activities including significant clinical/healthcare experience (often 500-2,000 hours), shadowing a physician assistant, and leadership/community service are also key components of preparation.

Students interested in veterinary medicine may choose any major they wish. They most often choose a major in the College of Agriculture, the College of Science, or the College of Health and Human Sciences. To be eligible for consideration for admission to the professional DVM program, students must complete at least 70-71 semester hours of undergraduate work. Required pre-requisite courses include: General Chemistry (8 credits), Organic Chemistry (8 credits), Biochemistry (3 credits), Biology (8 credits), Genetics (3 credits), Microbiology (4 credits), Physics (8 credits), Statistics (3 credits), English Composition (3 credits), Communication/Public Speaking (3 credits), and Humanities (9 credits). While it is possible to complete the pre-veterinary requirements in three years, most students complete a four-year baccalaureate degree program.

A student must complete 15 to 18 credit hours from the following: Core Courses (9 hours): CGT 22600 - Introduction To Constraint-Based Modeling, CGT 32600 - Manufacturing Graphics Standards, CGT 42600 - Product Lifecycle Management. Selectives (9 hours): Select three from the following: CGT 10301 - Geometric Modeling Concepts, CGT 11000 - Technical Graphics Communications, CGT 21500 - Computer Graphics Programming I, CGT 25001 - Computer Graphics Technology Standards, CGT 30302 - Virtual Product Integration, CGT 35102 - CGT Project Management, CGT 40301 - Product Data Management, CGT 45001 - Professional Practices, MET 14300 - 2D and 3D Tooling and Modeling, MET 24500 - Manufacturing Systems, MET 34600 - Advanced Product Development. Note: Students may use up to 6 credit hours of CGT courses towards both this minor and a CGT major.
The Professional Writing minor (PWRT) requires 15 credit hours. Students may not use more than two (2) courses from their major(s) to satisfy the requirements for this minor.

To be eligible for admission to the Professional Writing BA program, freshman applicants should have completed the following high school coursework: 8 semesters of English, 8 semesters of Math, 6 semesters of Lab Science, 6 semesters of Social Studies, and 4 semesters of a World Language. Purdue University is a test-required university; students must submit SAT or ACT scores. The application process also requires the Common Application and a personal essay.
Purdue University’s holistic application review process considers several factors: high school coursework, grades in core subjects, SAT or ACT scores, personal essay, and Purdue-specific questions.

To earn the Bachelor of Science degree in Psychological Sciences, students must complete a total of 120 credit hours. This includes the Purdue Core Curriculum, College of Health and Human Sciences (HHS) Core Requirements, and Psychological Sciences Departmental Requirements. Specific departmental requirements include core courses such as Introductory Psychology, Psychological Statistics, and Research Methods in Psychology, as well as several psychology electives.

The Psychology minor requires 15.00 credit hours. Required Course: PSY 12000 - Elementary Psychology (3 credits). Electives: Select 12 credits of PSY courses (Note: PSY 20100, 20300, 39000, 39100, 49100, 49200, 49600, 59100, 69000, 69100, and 69500 cannot be used to satisfy minor requirements). Additional Requirements: At least 6 credits must be 30000 level or higher. At least 9 credits must be from Purdue University. All PSY courses must be completed with a C- or better.

To apply for the Public Health, BS program, applicants must meet Purdue University's freshman admission criteria. This includes the completion of a high school curriculum with a minimum of 8 semesters of English, 8 semesters of Mathematics (including Algebra I, II, and Geometry), 6 semesters of Lab Science (including Biology and Chemistry), 6 semesters of Social Studies, and 4 semesters of a Foreign Language. Applicants must submit either SAT or ACT scores and complete the Common Application, which includes a personal essay and Purdue-specific writing prompts.

To apply for freshman admission to the Public Relations and Strategic Communication program, students must submit the Common Application, which includes a personal essay and Purdue-specific questions. Applicants must also provide high school transcripts (via self-reported course work) and are required to submit official SAT or ACT scores. Purdue uses a holistic review process that considers high school academic rigor, grades, and standardized test scores, as well as personal background and experiences.
Program name: Public Relations and Strategic Communication, BA

Requirements: Admission to the Quantitative Biology, BS program is based on a holistic review of several factors. Minimum high school course requirements include 8 semesters of English, 8 semesters of Mathematics (including pre-calculus or calculus for College of Science majors), 6 semesters of Lab Science (Biology, Chemistry, and Physics are recommended), 6 semesters of Social Studies, and 4 semesters of Foreign Language. Standardized test scores (SAT or ACT) are required for admission.
15-16 credits. Credits must be earned at Purdue. GPA must be 2.0 or higher. No more than 3 credits of 10000-level courses may count toward the minor.

The Radiological Health Sciences major provides a curriculum leading to a Bachelor of Science degree. Students select one of two concentrations: Health Physics or Pre-Medical Physics. The Pre-Medical Physics concentration is for students who wish to pursue a career as a medical physicist. This concentration provides students with a strong background in physics and mathematics, making them well-prepared for admission into a medical physics graduate program.

The Radiological Health Sciences major leads to the Bachelor of Science degree. Students select one of two concentrations: Health Physics or Pre-Medical Physics. Each concentration provides students with a strong foundation in physics, biology, and mathematics. To complete the Bachelor of Science degree, students must complete a minimum of 120 credit hours. For freshman admission, Purdue University requires SAT or ACT scores and expects applicants to have completed high school coursework including 8 semesters of English, 8 semesters of Math, 6 semesters of Lab Science, 6 semesters of Social Studies, and 4 semesters of Foreign Language.

The Real Estate major provides students with a strong foundation in real estate fundamentals, including real estate finance and investment, real estate development, and real estate law. To earn the BS degree with a major in Real Estate, students must complete a minimum of 120 credits. A 2.0 Graduation GPA is required for all courses taken at Purdue University and all courses taken in the Mitchell E. Daniels, Jr. School of Business. Application requirements include the submission of the Common Application, a personal essay, high school transcripts, and official SAT or ACT scores.

15 credits are required for the minor. Core Courses (3 credits): REL 20000 - Introduction To Religious Studies. Electives (12 credits): Choose 12 credits from the following list. No more than two courses from any one department can be used to satisfy the elective requirement. Note: REL 49900 - Directed Reading and REL 59000 - Directed Reading may count toward the Religious Studies minor with the permission of the Director of the Religious Studies Program.

To earn a Bachelor of Arts degree in the College of Liberal Arts, students shall satisfy the following requirements: 1. A minimum of 120 credit hours. 2. The College of Liberal Arts core requirements. 3. The Religious Studies major requirements. 4. A minimum of 32 credit hours at the 30000 level or above at Purdue University. General admission is based on a holistic review of the applicant's record including high school coursework (8 semesters of English, 8 semesters of Math, 6 semesters of Lab Science, 6 semesters of Social Studies, and 4 semesters of World Language), SAT or ACT scores, and a personal essay.

To apply for the Retail Management, BS program, applicants must submit an application through the Common App, which includes a personal essay and Purdue-specific questions. Applicants must provide self-reported high school grades and official SAT or ACT scores, as Purdue University is a test-required institution. The program requires the completion of 120 credit hours, including major-specific courses in Consumer Science (CSR) and core requirements from the College of Health and Human Sciences.

The robotics engineering technology (REGT) program prepares students for the challenges and opportunities of the 21st-century manufacturing and robotics-dependent industry. REGT combines mechanical, electrical, and computer engineering technology to provide students with a solid foundation in the principles and practices of robotics. The program requires 120 credit hours for graduation.
Students must complete 15 credit hours. Minimum GPA of 2.0 is required in all courses for the minor.

The Sales and Marketing major provides a curriculum for students who are interested in sales and marketing in the food, agribusiness, and general business industries. The curriculum focuses on preparing students for professional sales and marketing careers. It includes courses in economics, marketing, and professional selling, along with foundational courses in business, science, and the humanities. For admission, applicants must meet Purdue's freshman criteria, which include the completion of specific high school coursework (8 semesters of English and math, 6 semesters of lab science and social studies, and 4 semesters of a foreign language), submission of SAT or ACT scores, and a personal essay.

To be eligible for admission to the SSED program, students must meet the following requirements: 1. Completion of at least 30 credit hours of college-level coursework. 2. Minimum 2.50 overall GPA. 3. Minimum 3.00 average in Social Studies content courses. 4. Grades of C- or higher in all Social Studies content and Professional Education courses. 5. Satisfactory score on the CASA or equivalent (ACT/SAT/GRE) as required by the Indiana Department of Education. 6. Completion of EDCI 20500 and EDCI 28500.
15.00 Credit Hours. Required Courses: SOC 10000 - Introductory Sociology. Sociology Electives: 12 credits of Sociology courses, 9 of which must be at the 30000-level or above.

To earn a Bachelor of Science in Sociology, students must complete 120 total credits. This includes a 13-credit Sociology Core consisting of SOC 10000 (Introductory Sociology), SOC 38200 (Introduction To Statistics In Sociology), SOC 38300 (Introduction To Research Methods In Sociology), and SOC 40200 (Sociological Theory). Additionally, students must complete 18 credits of Sociology electives and the College of Liberal Arts Core Requirements. For undergraduate admission to Purdue University, applicants must submit the Common Application, which includes a personal essay and Purdue-specific questions, and self-report their high school grades and standardized test scores (SAT or ACT).

The program in Soil and Water Sciences is designed to provide students with a strong background in the basic sciences, with an emphasis on the chemistry, physics, and biology of the soil. Students take a core of courses that deal with soil-water-plant relations, soil chemistry, soil microbiology, and soil physics. These courses are supplemented by electives in the basic sciences and in related applied fields. The curriculum is flexible enough to allow students to prepare for careers in environmental consulting, soil and water conservation, land use, or for graduate study. Completion of the program provides the student with the necessary course work to be a Certified Professional Soil Scientist. General freshman admission requires a high school transcript, a personal essay, and SAT or ACT scores.

Successful audition/interview/portfolio review is required for admission to this major. Students must complete a portfolio review and interview. To schedule an interview/review, applicants should contact the Theatre department. General Purdue University admission requirements also apply, including the Common Application personal statement and high school transcripts. Purdue University is a test-required institution; SAT or ACT scores are required for admission.
Program name: Sound for the Performing Arts, BA

Requirements: Minimum Credits: 15. A minimum of 6 credit hours must be taken in residence at the West Lafayette campus. At least one of the SPAN 40000-level courses must be taken in residence at the West Lafayette campus. A grade of C- or better is required in all courses for the minor. Minimum GPA: 2.00.

Students must complete 12 credits of SPAN coursework at the 30000-level or above. All courses must be taught in Spanish. At least 6 credits must be completed on the West Lafayette campus. All courses must be completed with a C- or better.

Candidates must complete a minimum of 120 credit hours for the Bachelor of Arts degree. The Spanish major specifically requires 30 credit hours of Spanish courses above the 20200 level, with a minimum grade of C- in all major courses. At least 15 of these 30 credit hours must be completed on the Purdue West Lafayette campus. General undergraduate admission requires the submission of official high school transcripts, a personal essay (Statement of Purpose), and SAT or ACT scores.

The program requires a total of 120 credit hours and a minimum graduation GPA of 2.80. Students must be admitted to the Teacher Education Program (TEP) and complete all professional education and content courses with a grade of C or better. General undergraduate admission to Purdue University requires the submission of high school transcripts, SAT or ACT scores, and a personal essay.
Program name: Special Education Dual Licensure: Elementary Education and Mild Intervention P-12, BA

Requirements: Admission to the Professional Education Program: 1. Minimum 3.0 overall GPA (subject to change). 2. No grade lower than a 'C-' in any course required for the major. 3. Current, valid ‘Expanded’ Criminal Background Check on file with the Office of Field Experiences. 4. Completion of required Teacher Education foundation courses.

The SLHS major provides a scientific foundation for students interested in careers in the fields of speech-language pathology, audiology, and other health related fields. Enrollment in the SLHS major is open to any student who is in good standing with the University. For a student to remain in good standing in the SLHS major, they must maintain a cumulative GPA of 2.000 or higher. A student who falls below a cumulative 2.000 GPA will be placed on SLHS departmental probation. Students must have a 2.000 cumulative GPA in all courses to graduate.
Program name: Speech, Language, and Hearing Sciences, BS

Requirements: Freshman applicants are evaluated based on several criteria including: high school coursework (8 semesters of English, 8 semesters of math, 6 semesters of natural science, 6 semesters of social studies, and 4 semesters of a foreign language), grades in academic courses, SAT or ACT scores, a personal essay, and Purdue-specific questions. For the College of Science, completion of calculus is highly recommended.

The Mathematics and Statistics program is a joint program between the Department of Mathematics and the Department of Statistics. It is designed to provide students with a strong background in both mathematics and statistics. For admission, freshman applicants must submit the Common Application, which includes a personal essay and Purdue-specific questions. Applicants to the College of Science are expected to have completed 8 semesters of Mathematics (including pre-calculus or calculus), 8 semesters of English, 6 semesters of Lab Science, 6 semesters of Social Studies, and 4 semesters of a single Foreign Language. Purdue University requires SAT or ACT scores for undergraduate admission.

Admission to the Studio Arts and Design, BA program is based on Purdue University's general freshman admission criteria, which include completion of the high school Core 40 curriculum (or equivalent), SAT or ACT scores, and a personal essay. According to the Patti & Rusty Rueff School of Design, Art, and Performance, no portfolio is required for freshman admission to the Studio Arts and Design major.

Students are admitted to the Mitchell E. Daniels, Jr. School of Business as first-year students. Factors that are considered in the admission process include: High school course expectations, High school GPA, SAT/ACT scores, and Personal background and experiences. In addition, students may also apply for admission as a transfer student from either another college or university or from another academic unit at Purdue University (CODO). Transfer students from outside of Purdue University must have at least a 3.0 or higher GPA and must have completed at least 12 credit hours.
Program name: Supply Chain and Operations Management, BS

Requirements: Purdue University has a holistic admissions process. Evaluation is based on several factors, including: High School Coursework (including meeting minimum subject requirements: 8 semesters of English, 8 semesters of Math, 6 semesters of Lab Science, etc.), Grades in High School Coursework, Strength of your overall high school curriculum, Overall grades (GPA), SAT or ACT test scores, Personal Essay, and Evidence of motivation, leadership, and service.

To apply for the BS in Sustainable Biomaterials-Process and Product Design, applicants must meet Purdue University’s general undergraduate admission requirements. Admission is based on a holistic review of high school coursework (including 8 semesters of English, 8 semesters of math, 6 semesters of lab science, 6 semesters of social studies, and 4 semesters of a single world language), grades, official SAT or ACT scores, and a personal essay with Purdue-specific writing prompts. The degree program itself requires the completion of 120 credit hours, including core courses in biology, chemistry, math, physics, and specialized forestry and natural resources (FNR) courses.
Program name: Sustainable Biomaterials-Process and Product Design, BS

Requirements: To apply for the Sustainable Food and Farming Systems, BS program, students must meet Purdue University's freshman admission criteria, which include a minimum of 8 semesters of English, 8 semesters of Mathematics, 6 semesters of Lab Science, 6 semesters of Social Studies, and 4 semesters of Foreign Language. A personal essay and Purdue-specific responses are required as part of the application. The program itself requires a minimum of 120 credits for graduation, including the University Core Curriculum and College of Agriculture requirements, with specific coursework in Biology, Chemistry, and Mathematics (Calculus or Statistics).
Program name: Sustainable Food and Farming Systems, BS

Requirements: Admission to Purdue University is based on a holistic review of each application. For freshman admission, Purdue requires the Common Application and a personal essay. Applicants must meet high school coursework requirements, which include 8 semesters of English, 8 semesters of mathematics (including precalculus or calculus for most Polytechnic programs), 6 semesters of laboratory science, 6 semesters of social studies, and 4 semesters of a single foreign language. Additionally, Purdue University is test-required; SAT or ACT scores are expected for all students applying for freshman admission.

To complete the Teaching Physical Education/Health, BA program, students must earn a total of 120.00 semester hours. A minimum GPA of 2.80 is required for all Professional Education and Content courses. Additionally, all Professional Education and Content courses must be completed with a grade of C- or higher. Students completing this program will be eligible for Indiana licensure in Physical Education (P-12) and Health (P-12).

To apply for the Turf Management and Science, BS program, applicants must meet Purdue University’s freshman admission criteria, which include the completion of a high school curriculum with 8 semesters of English, 8 semesters of Mathematics, 6 semesters of Laboratory Science, 6 semesters of Social Studies, and 4 semesters of World Language. Applicants are required to submit SAT or ACT scores and a personal statement (Common App essay). The program requires a minimum of 120 credit hours for graduation, including core coursework in Agronomy and Turfgrass Science.

To apply for freshman admission, you must submit: The Common Application, Purdue-specific questions (including those about your choice of major), Self-reported high school grades, and Self-reported SAT or ACT test scores.

Admission to the User Experience (UX) Design program at Purdue University requires the submission of a completed Common Application, including a personal essay and Purdue-specific short-answer questions. For the current application cycle, Purdue University requires self-reported SAT or ACT scores from all freshman applicants. High school course expectations include 8 semesters of English, 8 semesters of Mathematics (including Algebra I, II, Geometry, and a higher-level math course), 6 semesters of Laboratory Science, 6 semesters of Social Studies, and 4 semesters of a single Foreign Language. The program itself requires 120 credit hours and a minimum cumulative GPA of 2.0 for graduation.

Admission to the Veterinary Nursing Program is competitive. Selection is based on several factors, including: academic performance in the required prerequisite courses, overall academic performance (Cumulative GPA), a minimum of 40 hours of practical experience with a veterinarian, and a personal statement/essay.

To earn the Bachelor of Science (BS) degree in Virtual Product Integration, students must complete 120 credit hours with a minimum 2.0 Graduation GPA. Application requirements for undergraduate freshman admission include the Common App personal essay, high school transcripts, and self-reported or official SAT or ACT scores. Completion of a college-prep high school curriculum is expected, including 8 semesters of English, 8 semesters of Math, 6 semesters of Lab Science, 6 semesters of Social Studies, and 4 semesters of a Foreign Language.

To apply for undergraduate programs at Purdue University, including Web Programming and Design, applicants must submit the Common App, which includes a personal essay and Purdue-specific questions. Required documents include official high school transcripts and self-reported or official SAT or ACT scores. Admission is based on a holistic review of academic performance, including core subject requirements (4 years of English, 4 years of Math, 3 years of Lab Science, 3 years of Social Studies, and 2 years of Foreign Language).

The welding engineering technology (WET) program is intended to produce graduates who are prepared to handle the responsibilities and requirements of a welding engineer. Graduates of this program will be experts in the application and implementation of welding technology. They will have the skills and knowledge to oversee the implementation of the equipment, procedures, and quality control. Admission to the program requires meeting Purdue University's freshman admission criteria, which includes the completion of specific high school coursework (8 semesters of English, 8 semesters of Math, 6 semesters of Lab Science, 6 semesters of Social Studies, and 4 semesters of Foreign Language), submission of SAT or ACT scores, and a personal essay. A total of 124 semester hours are required for the degree.

Admission to the Wildlife, BS program is based on a holistic review of several factors. Required high school coursework includes 8 semesters of English, 8 semesters of Mathematics (including Algebra I, II, and Geometry), 6 semesters of Laboratory Science (including Biology, Chemistry, or Physics), 6 semesters of Social Studies, and 4 semesters of a Foreign Language. Additionally, applicants must submit SAT or ACT scores, a personal essay, and answers to Purdue-specific questions. Evaluation also considers the applicant's GPA and the strength of their high school curriculum.

The Women’s, Gender, and Sexuality Studies (WGSS) major consists of 33 credit hours of coursework. Students must also complete the College of Liberal Arts Core Requirements and the University Core Curriculum. All courses for the major must be completed with a grade of C- or better.
Program name: Women's, Gender, and Sexuality Studies, BA
